findings.suggestedPatch: Smallest first step, one line and no type change: mirror the priority guard on line 74 — `rating: status === 'Finished' ? rating : 0` — so an unread book carries no fabricated score. That alone fixes the export and the status toggle. The structural fix, for the same file plus types.ts, is to make Book a two-arm discriminated union on `status`: `type Book = BookBase & ({ status: 'Finished'; rating: number; finishedAt?: string } | { status: 'Want to Read'; priority?: Priority })`, which would make line 74 a compile error and would also retire the dead `finishedAt`. HONEST COST: that union touches every producer (AddBookModal, useLibrary.importGoodreadsRows, migrate.ts, summarize.toGenerated, the repo tests) and every consumer that reads `rating` or `priority` without first narrowing on `status` (BookCard, BookDetail, StatsView, markdown.ts, LibraryPage's sort) — roughly a dozen files. Do the one-line guard now and log the union as a structural recommendation.

plain.title: Books you have not read are saved with a rating of four stars that you never gave
plain.what: The add-book form knows that ratings only apply to finished books, because it hides the rating control otherwise. It still saves the control's default value for every book regardless.
plain.whyItMatters: Every want-to-read book is stored with a phantom four-star rating that appears in exports, is treated as real when the status is later changed, and drags the average-rating statistic upward.
plain.whatToDo: Apply the same status check to the rating that is already applied to the priority, so an unread book carries no fabricated score.

findings.title: togglePlay ignores the Promise returned by play() — the same call is caught 21 lines above — and flips isPlaying unconditionally, so the UI shows Pause while nothing is playing
findings.description: `HTMLMediaElement.play()` is declared `Promise<void>` and rejects routinely: NotAllowedError when autoplay policy blocks a gesture-less play, AbortError when `src` changes mid-load, NotSupportedError on a bad blob URL. The file already knows this — line 29 attaches `.catch((e) => console.error('Autoplay failed', e))` to the identical call. `togglePlay` at lines 45-54 does not, so the rejection is unhandled. Worse, `setIsPlaying(!isPlaying)` on line 52 runs regardless of whether playback actually started, so the type-level 'this succeeded' assumption leaks into state: the button renders the Pause icon and the progress bar sits at 0 while nothing plays, and the user has no way to tell the difference from a stalled stream. Exact input: a generated WAV whose blob URL has already been revoked, or any environment where the play attempt is rejected. Broken consumer: the AudioPlayer's own render (lines 190-194), which trusts `isPlaying`.
findings.suggestedPatch: Make the state follow the outcome rather than the intention: `audioRef.current.play().then(() => setIsPlaying(true)).catch(() => setIsPlaying(false))` on line 50, and move the `setIsPlaying(!isPlaying)` on line 52 into the pause branch only. The existing `onPlay`/`onPause` handlers (lines 117-118) already sync state from the element, so this mainly removes the optimistic flip. Risk: none — the element's own events remain the source of truth.

plain.title: The audio player shows Pause when nothing is actually playing
plain.what: Pressing play flips the button to Pause without waiting to see whether playback actually started. The result of the attempt is discarded, even though the same call is handled properly twenty lines above.
plain.whyItMatters: When the browser blocks playback — a common autoplay restriction — the user sees a Pause button, hears nothing, and pressing it again does nothing useful.
plain.whatToDo: Set the playing state from the outcome of the attempt rather than from the intention.

findings.title: BookDetail reads the Summary's takeaway while BookCard reads the denormalised copy, and they visibly disagree
findings.description: The same fact is stored twice with different types and no invariant tying them: `Summary.oneSentenceTakeaway` is required `string` (types.ts:57) and `Book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is optional `string` (types.ts:48). BookDetail line 452 renders the Summary copy; `BookCard.tsx:89` renders the Book copy with a falsy fallback (`book.oneSentenceTakeaway ? ... : 'Not summarised yet'`). Nothing keeps them in sync: `book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is written ONLY at creation time (`AddBookModal.tsx:72`, `LibraryPage.tsx:92`), and `saveSummary` (useLibrary.tsx:78-88) syncs only `book.summaryId` back onto the book - never the takeaway. WHAT THE USER SEES: a book whose stored `oneSentenceTakeaway` is `''` (migrate.ts:125 writes exactly that for legacy records, and any imported backup can carry it) has a real Summary with `summaryId` set, yet its BookCard says 'Not summarised yet' in the library while opening it shows the genuine takeaway quoted in the orange panel - the library and the detail view contradict each other about the same book. The optional-vs-required typing is what permits it: the compiler cannot express 'if `summaryId` is set then `oneSentenceTakeaway` is a non-empty string'. FIX SHAPE: fold the denormalised fields into the tagged union proposed in L11-F02 so they can only be absent together, and have `saveSummary` write the takeaway back onto the Book whenever the Summary changes. Note the denormalisation itself is deliberate (CLAUDE.md) and should be kept - only the sync and the typing need fixing.
findings.verifierNote: The contradiction is real and I confirm it, but the mechanism the discoverer identified is the wrong one and the true mechanism is deterministic rather than conditional — amending the description, keeping the severity. VERIFIED: `Summary.oneSentenceTakeaway` is required `string` (src/types.ts:57) while `Book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is optional `string` (src/types.ts:48). src/components/BookDetail.tsx:452 renders the Summary copy (`{summary ? `"${summary.oneSentenceTakeaway}"` : ''}`) and src/components/BookCard.tsx:89 renders the Book copy with a falsy fallback (`{book.oneSentenceTakeaway ? `"${book.oneSentenceTakeaway}"` : 'Not summarised yet'}`) — both verbatim. An exhaustive grep for `oneSentenceTakeaway` confirms `book.oneSentenceTakeaway` has exactly TWO writers, both at creation time: src/components/AddBookModal.tsx:72 and src/features/library/LibraryPage.tsx:92. `saveSummary` (src/features/library/useLibrary.tsx:78-88) syncs only `summaryId` and never the takeaway — and per this audit's established baseline its backfill at lines 82-83 is dead code anyway. CORRECTION TO THE MECHANISM: the discoverer blamed src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:125, but that line writes the SUMMARY's takeaway (`oneSentenceTakeaway: legacy.oneSentenceTakeaway ?? ''`), not the Book's. The actual violation is at src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:105-119, where `books.create({...})` sets `summaryId` (line 117) but OMITS `oneSentenceTakeaway` entirely — the field is not in the object literal at all. It compiles because the field is optional. So `book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is `undefined` for 100% of migrated legacy books, not just for the subset whose legacy takeaway was empty. Every legacy user therefore sees 'Not summarised yet' on every card in their library while opening any of those books shows the genuine takeaway in the orange panel — the two views contradict each other about every migrated book, deterministically. That is strictly stronger than the reported ''-valued case and matches this audit's already-established correction that the invariant is violated for real at migrate.ts:105-119. The type angle is legitimate and not a pattern-match: `oneSentenceTakeaway?` being optional while `summaryId?` is independently optional is exactly what lets migrate.ts construct the impossible state and compile. Severity stays `medium` — a durable, deterministic, user-visible inconsistency, but cosmetic in consequence (no crash, no data loss).
findings.reachability: Deterministic on the legacy-migration path, which every pre-IndexedDB user hits exactly once. `migrateLegacyData` (src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:80) runs when `booksum_library_*` keys exist and the `booksum.migratedAt` marker is unset (lines 81-84); every book it creates gets `summaryId` but no `oneSentenceTakeaway`. Books added via AddBookModal or the recommendation preview are unaffected (both writers set the field). Goodreads-imported books are self-consistent — useLibrary.tsx:150-160 sets neither `summaryId` nor the takeaway — and I confirmed BookDetail offers no 'summarise this existing book' action (BookDetail.tsx:183 bails with `if (!summary) return`), so they cannot drift into the inconsistent state.
findings.blastRadius: One denormalised field, 2 writers (AddBookModal.tsx:72, LibraryPage.tsx:92) and 3 readers (BookCard.tsx:89 reads the Book copy; BookDetail.tsx:452 and DailyWisdomModal.tsx:60 read the Summary copy). Affects every book row rendered in the library grid and in StatsView for migrated profiles. src/lib/storage/migrate.test.ts exists but asserts on the Summary side, not on `book.oneSentenceTakeaway`.

plain.title: The book page and the library card read two different copies of the same sentence
plain.what: The one-sentence takeaway is stored twice: once on the summary and once copied onto the book. Nothing keeps the two in step.
plain.whyItMatters: For migrated books the two visibly disagree — the library says 'Not summarised yet' while the detail page shows the sentence.
plain.whatToDo: Fix the missing copy first, then decide whether the duplicate field is worth keeping at all.

findings.title: Chat Message has no error variant, so a failure is rendered as if the assistant said it — and if the stream already emitted one chunk, the error is dropped entirely
findings.description: CONSTRUCTIBLE IMPOSSIBLE STATE: a `Message` with `role: 'model'` whose `text` is an AiError string rather than model output. `interface Message { role: 'user' | 'model'; text: string }` (lines 15-18) has no third arm and no status field, so the catch block at 70-79 has nowhere to put a failure and overwrites the streaming placeholder's text instead. TWO DISTINCT CONSUMER FAILURES, both reachable: (1) When the request fails before any chunk arrives (no API key, offline, 429), the placeholder's text is replaced with `toAiError(err).message` and the renderer at lines 140-152 paints it in the orange assistant bubble behind the Sparkles avatar, styled identically to a real answer — the user cannot distinguish 'Could not reach Google. Check your connection and try again.' from something the book assistant asserted. (2) Worse, when the stream fails *after* emitting at least one chunk, the replace predicate `entry.role === 'model' && entry.text === ''` (line 75) no longer matches — the placeholder's text is non-empty by then — so `.map` returns the array unchanged and the error message is silently discarded. `sendMessageStream` (chat.ts:29-38) calls `onChunk(text)` inside the `for await` loop and rethrows anything the iterator raises, so a mid-stream safety block or dropped connection lands exactly here. `isLoading` then flips false in the `finally` and the user is left looking at a truncated half-sentence with no indication anything went wrong. The type gives no hint that `text` carries two different kinds of value.
findings.suggestedPatch: Smallest first step, contained entirely in ChatModal.tsx: add the missing arm to the local type — `type Message = { role: 'user'; text: string } | { role: 'model'; text: string; failed?: true }` — then in the catch, drop the `entry.text === ''` predicate and replace the last model entry with `{ ...entry, text: entry.text ? entry.text + '\n\n' + message : message, failed: true }`, and in the renderer branch on `msg.failed` to use the error styling the app already has (the red panel at ApiKeyDialog.tsx:66 is the existing precedent). `Message` is declared locally and used nowhere else in the repo, so this touches one file and no other producer or consumer.

plain.title: A chat failure is displayed as though the assistant said it, or is dropped entirely
plain.what: The chat message format has only two kinds, user and assistant, with no way to represent a failure. An error is therefore written into an assistant message.
plain.whyItMatters: The user cannot tell an error apart from a real answer, it becomes part of the conversation history sent to the model, and if the reply had already started streaming the error is discarded and the partial answer is left looking complete.
plain.whatToDo: Add a failure variant to the message type and render it distinctly, so errors are never mistaken for answers.

findings.title: `pages[currentPage]` is typed `string` but can be `undefined`, crashing the reader on a whitespace-only deep dive
findings.description: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off (tsconfig.json:2-18 sets `strict: true` and nothing more), so `pages[currentPage]` at EReader.tsx:395 types as a definite `string` and satisfies `RenderFormattedContent`'s `content: string` (line 53) even when the index is out of range. The memo at lines 182-190 can genuinely return `[]`: `generateDetailedSummary` guards only the empty string (`return text || 'Failed to generate detailed summary.'`, summarize.ts:99), so a whitespace-only stream is stored as `detailedSummary`, passes the truthy check at line 183, and is reduced to `[]` by `.split(/(?=## )/g).map(trim).filter(Boolean)`. Verified by execution: `pages[0]` is then `undefined` and `content.split('\n')` at line 58 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')`, killing the /book/:id/read route into the error boundary; line 457 emits `width: 'Infinity%'` and line 461 renders 'Infinity% Complete'. The failure is durable because the bad `detailedSummary` is persisted. NOTE: the originally claimed second trigger — `currentPage` dangling after the memo shrinks mid-session — is not reachable; `pages` depends only on `summary?.detailedSummary` (line 190) and ReaderPage.tsx:9 never mutates the summary. Fix shape: return the placeholder page when `sections` is empty, and clamp `currentPage` into range; enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` separately as a repo-wide change.
findings.verifierNote:
Pattern confirmed exactly, reachability narrower than claimed, and the second trigger is refuted. CONFIRMED: EReader.tsx:395 passes `pages[currentPage]` into `content: string` (declared at line 53) which is dereferenced at line 58 `content.split('
')`; the memo at 182-190 can return `[]`; tsconfig.json:8 sets `strict: true` with no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and no `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (both absent from the file), so `pages[currentPage]` types as a definite `string`. I reproduced the full chain in node: `'

  '` passes the truthy guard at line 183, `.split(/(?=## )/g).map(trim).filter(Boolean)` yields `[]`, `pages[0]` is `undefined`, and `content.split` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')`; the progress bar computes `Infinity` (line 457) and line 461 renders 'Infinity% Complete'. The producer note is off by two lines — the fallback is summarize.ts:99 (`return text || 'Failed to generate detailed summary.'`), not :97 — but the point stands: it screens the empty string, not a whitespace-only stream. REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: 'any shrink of the memo while the reader is mounted leaves the index dangling'. `pages` depends only on `summary?.detailedSummary` (line 190) and ReaderPage.tsx:9 never takes `setSummary`, while useBookRoute.ts:21 sets the summary once per book — the reader cannot shrink its own page list mid-session. AMENDED TO MEDIUM: the only live trigger requires Gemini to stream content that is non-empty but entirely whitespace, a narrow model-output edge rather than a routinely-exercised path. The type weakness and the trivial fix are real; the crash probability does not clear the 'critical business path / routinely exercised' bar for high.
findings.reachability: Only via a Gemini stream whose accumulated text is non-empty but whitespace-only: BookDetail.tsx:184 stores it, BookDetailPage.tsx:46 persists it via saveSummary, then /book/:id/read mounts EReader and the render throws into the error boundary. Durable once persisted — reopening the reader crashes again until the summary is regenerated, and there is no regenerate action (BookDetail.tsx:176 short-circuits when detailedSummary exists).
findings.blastRadius: Local: `pages` is used at EReader.tsx:219, 395, 405, 457, 461, 468 within one component; one mount site (ReaderPage.tsx:23). Enabling noUncheckedIndexedAccess repo-wide is the broad-radius variant of the same fix.

plain.title: The reader can crash on a deep dive that is only whitespace
plain.what: The reader assumes its page list is never empty. A deep dive made only of blank lines produces an empty list, and the reader then tries to render a page that does not exist.
plain.whyItMatters: The reading view fails outright, taking the surrounding screen with it, for a summary the AI produced with no visible content.
plain.whatToDo: Make the fallback guarantee real by returning the placeholder page when the split produces nothing.

findings.title: pages is inferred string[] but .filter(Boolean) can yield an empty array, so pages[currentPage] is undefined while typed string and crashes RenderFormattedContent
findings.description:
The `pages` useMemo is inferred as `string[]`, and the `['No content available.']` fallback on line 183 shows the author intended a non-empty guarantee. The guarantee does not hold: the fallback only fires when `detailedSummary` is falsy, so a whitespace-only `detailedSummary` passes the check and then `.map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)` reduces it to `[]` (verified in node). With `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` off, `pages[currentPage]` at line 395 is typed `string` while holding `undefined`, and it is handed to `RenderFormattedContent`'s required `content: string` prop, whose first statement is `content.split('
')` -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')` (verified). Exact input: a `detailedSummary` of `'   '` or `'

'`. That is reachable because `generateDetailedSummary` (summarize.ts:99) returns `text || 'Failed to...'` — a whitespace-only stream is truthy, so it is returned and persisted verbatim as a real deep-dive. Broken consumer: ReaderPage -> EReader throws during render, and react-router's errorElement replaces the whole app; the progress bar on line 457 also divides by `pages.length` of 0.
findings.suggestedPatch: Make the non-empty guarantee real at line 189: `return sections.length > 0 ? sections : ['No content available.'];`. Optionally also clamp the index at line 395 (`pages[Math.min(currentPage, pages.length - 1)] ?? ''`) so a shrinking `pages` from a summary update cannot leave `currentPage` past the end. Risk: none — it is a one-line widening of an existing fallback.

plain.title: A whitespace-only deep dive produces an empty reader that crashes on open
plain.what: The reader builds its page list and falls back to a placeholder only when the text is entirely missing. Text made only of blank lines passes that check and then produces no pages at all.
plain.whyItMatters: Opening the reader on such a summary fails outright and takes the surrounding screen down with it. The AI can produce such a summary.
plain.whatToDo: Apply the placeholder fallback after the pages are built, not before, so the non-empty guarantee is real.

findings.title: `correctAnswerIndex` is used as an index into `options` with no bounds relationship in the type; an out-of-range index silently makes the quiz unwinnable
findings.description: `QuizQuestion` (types.ts:105-110) models `options: string[]` and `correctAnswerIndex: number` as two independent fields — nothing in the type ties the index to the array's bounds, and nothing validates it (the producer is quiz.ts:16, see F016). QuizModal renders correctness by comparing the rendered option's position to that index (QuizModal.tsx:183) and scores by the same comparison (line 78). Failure scenario: the model returns `options: ['A','B','C']` with `correctAnswerIndex: 3`, or 1-based indices, since schemas.ts:69-72 only *describes* 'Index (0-3)' and 'Array of 4 possible answers' in prose. `isCorrect` is then false for every rendered option — no green highlight (lines 190-191, 219), whichever answer the user picks is styled wrong (192-193), `setScore` never fires, and the finish screen reports '0%' and 'You answered 0 out of N correctly!' (lines 146-149). The app looks broken and blames the user. SCOPE: this is the transient face of the same boundary defect as F016 — nothing here is persisted (the durable write is QuizModal.tsx:52-61), so the harm ends when the modal closes, which is why this is medium while F016 stays high. Correction to the original note: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` would NOT have caught this site — QuizModal never evaluates `options[correctAnswerIndex]`, it only compares `idx === correctAnswerIndex`. Fix shape: validate the index at the `generateBookQuiz` boundary (fixing both consumers at once); longer term an `{ options, correctAnswer: string }` shape removes the class of bug entirely.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern and failure scenario confirmed; severity lowered because this is the transient twin of F016. VERIFIED at current lines: types.ts:105-110 models `options: string[]` and `correctAnswerIndex: number` as independent fields with no bounds relationship; QuizModal.tsx:183 `const isCorrect = idx === questions[currentQuestionIndex].correctAnswerIndex` drives every option's styling (189-220), line 78 scores by the same comparison, line 93 computes the percentage, line 182 maps the options. With an out-of-range index (or the classic 1-based-index model failure) `isCorrect` is false for every rendered option: no green highlight (190-191, 219), whichever option the user picks is styled wrong (192-193), `setScore` never fires, and lines 146-149 report '0%' / 'You answered 0 out of N correctly!'. AMENDED TO MEDIUM: this is the same root cause as F016 (unvalidated Gemini output, quiz.ts:16) at a different consumer, and F017's INDEPENDENT impact is confined to one modal session — nothing is persisted by lines 78/93/182/183; the durable harm belongs to F016's write at lines 52-61, which already carries high. Rating both at high double-counts one boundary defect. Minor inaccuracy in the description: the `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` remark cites `options[correctAnswerIndex]`, an expression QuizModal never evaluates — it only compares `idx === correctAnswerIndex`, so that flag would not have caught this particular site.
findings.reachability: Same entry as F016 — open a summarised book, click 'Quiz' — but the visible effect here (an unwinnable, always-0% quiz) lasts only as long as the modal is open. Requires the model to return an index outside `[0, options.length)`, which the schema at schemas.ts:69-72 does not prevent.
findings.blastRadius: Four expressions inside one component (QuizModal.tsx:78, 93, 182, 183), one modal session, no persistence. The shared `QuizQuestion` type (types.ts:105-110) has 3 referencing modules (quiz.ts:6, QuizModal.tsx:4, types.ts), and the identical unbounded-index shape is mirrored on `ReviewCard` (types.ts:88-89).
findings.suggestedPatch: No separate patch needed — the boundary guard in F016's `suggestedPatch` (src/lib/ai/quiz.ts:16-17, dropping questions where `Number.isInteger(correctAnswerIndex) && correctAnswerIndex >= 0 && correctAnswerIndex < options.length` fails) fixes this consumer too, because `questions` at QuizModal.tsx:45 is set from the same return value. Land F016's fix and re-verify this one. If a defence-in-depth change is wanted in the component, make the empty state honest rather than adding a cast: QuizModal.tsx:45 `setQuestions(quizData)` unchanged, relying on the existing 'Could not generate quiz.' branch at lines 125-137 which already handles a zero-length list. Risk: none; the only behaviour change is fewer, valid questions instead of an unwinnable one.

plain.title: The quiz screen uses the answer position as a list index with nothing guaranteeing it fits
plain.what: The quiz reads the answer choices by position using a number that has never been checked against the size of the list.
plain.whyItMatters: An out-of-range value makes the quiz unwinnable, and the user is told they were wrong every time with no explanation.
plain.whatToDo: No separate change is needed here; validating the AI output where it is produced fixes this site too.

findings.title: `Book.rating: number` conflates "unrated" with "rated 0", so the average-rating stat is silently wrong for imported libraries
findings.description: Same defect as filed, re-categorised. `Book.rating: number` has no representation for 'unrated', so goodreads.ts:111 encodes absence as the sentinel 0; StatsView.tsx:20 averages it in and reports a false 'Avg. Rating' after any Goodreads import, BookCard.tsx:100 prints an authoritative '0/5', and BookDetail.tsx:215 (`book.rating || 5`) turns the sentinel into an invented 5-star rating when the book is marked Finished. The fix is an explicit absent state (optional field or tagged rating), not a brand.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern and data flow confirmed on every cited line. types.ts:36 `rating: number` is required with no 'unrated' representation; goodreads.ts:111 substitutes the sentinel `rating: Number.isFinite(rating) ? rating : 0` (Goodreads exports write 0 for unrated); goodreads.ts:74-76 `toStatus` maps shelf 'read' -> 'Finished', so read-but-unrated rows land in exactly the set StatsView averages. StatsView.tsx:20 reduces `b.rating` over all Finished books with no filter; BookCard.tsx:100 renders `{book.rating}/5` for every Finished book. Secondary claim also holds: StatsView.tsx:18-21 yields `string | number` (`.toFixed(1)` vs the literal `0`), which is why StatCard.value is widened to `string | number` at StatsView.tsx:197. One more consequence the discovery missed, which strengthens it: BookDetail.tsx:215 does `rating: newStatus === 'Finished' ? book.rating || 5 : book.rating`, so marking an unrated import Finished silently fabricates a 5-star rating out of the sentinel. Severity stays medium (wrong displayed data, no crash). Category amended: this is not two same-typed domain concepts being swapped (the branded-type definition) but a missing 'unrated' state, so discriminated-union-opportunity is the accurate bucket and keeps the report's branded-type section honest.
findings.reachability: Import a Goodreads CSV containing read-but-unrated rows (the default for most large exports) -> the Stats headline 'Avg. Rating' is dragged toward 0 and every such book's card shows '0/5'. Marking any of them Finished from BookDetail.tsx:215 converts the sentinel into a fabricated 5.
findings.blastRadius: 3 render/derivation sites (StatsView.tsx:20 + :93, BookCard.tsx:100, BookDetail.tsx:278-287) plus 2 writers (goodreads.ts:111, BookDetail.tsx:215).
findings.suggestedPatch: types.ts:36 -> `rating?: number;` (absent = unrated). goodreads.ts:111 -> `...(Number.isFinite(rating) && rating > 0 ? { rating } : {})`. StatsView.tsx:18-21 -> `const rated = finished.filter((b) => (b.rating ?? 0) > 0); const avgRating = rated.length ? (rated.reduce((a, b) => a + (b.rating ?? 0), 0) / rated.length).toFixed(1) : '--';` (always a string, so StatCard.value narrows to `string`). BookCard.tsx:100 -> render the badge only when rating is set. Risk: making `rating` optional touches every Book literal (repo create calls, test fixtures) - mechanical, but compile-wide.

plain.title: A rating of zero means 'unrated', so the average rating statistic is wrong after any import
plain.what: Book ratings use zero to mean 'not rated', but the statistics screen averages every book including those zeros.
plain.whyItMatters: Importing an unrated Goodreads library drags the displayed average rating toward zero and presents it as a real figure.
plain.whatToDo: Make 'unrated' an absent value rather than a zero, and exclude unrated books from the average.

findings.title: `querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>` is an unchecked assertion over a runtime selector string in the app's shared focus trap
findings.description: `querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>` at useFocusTrap.ts:18 is an assertion, not a check - the compiler never validates the selector at :5 - and it asserts nothing about visibility. Correction to the discovery rationale: the app renders no inline `<a>` and no `tabindex` attribute, so the SVGAElement mismatch is not reachable. The live defect is hidden controls: AddBookModal.tsx:229 renders a display:none file input inside the Dialog and its submit button is disabled at :264-266, so that hidden input becomes the last focusable, `active === last` at useFocusTrap.ts:54 never holds, and Tab escapes the modal.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern confirmed at useFocusTrap.ts:18 - `querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(FOCUSABLE)` is an unchecked generic assertion; the compiler never parses the selector at :5. Half the discovery rationale is wrong: grep for `<a ` across src/**/*.tsx returns ZERO inline anchors and there is no `tabIndex` attribute anywhere in the app, so no SVG node can match `a[href]` or `[tabindex]` and the SVGAElement scenario is unreachable. The visibility half is real, and I found the concrete site: AddBookModal.tsx:229-235 renders `<input type="file" className="hidden">` (display:none) inside a Dialog, and in upload mode with no file chosen the submit button at :262-266 is `disabled` and therefore excluded by `button:not([disabled])`. The hidden input is then the LAST entry in `focusable()`, so `last` at useFocusTrap.ts:48 can never equal `document.activeElement`, the forward-Tab wrap at :54-57 never fires, and Tab escapes the aria-modal dialog - the exact guarantee the hook exists to provide. Severity stays medium (accessibility degradation, no crash). The two `!` at :47-48 are guarded by `if (items.length === 0) return;` at :45, consistent with earlier batches.
findings.reachability: Add book -> 'Upload PDF' tab -> Tab forward past the last visible control: focus leaves the modal instead of wrapping, because the disabled submit is filtered out and the display:none file input is last. Same shape in the Goodreads tab (GoodreadsImport.tsx:64-70 hidden input) whenever the import button at :98 is disabled.
findings.blastRadius: Single shared trap for every modal surface: Dialog.tsx:19 (AddBookModal.tsx:100, ApiKeyDialog, ConfirmDialog.tsx:39) plus ChatModal, QuizModal and DailyWisdomModal calling it directly - 6 surfaces, 1 with a proven live failure.
findings.suggestedPatch: useFocusTrap.ts:17-20 -> `() => Array.from(panelRef.current?.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE) ?? []).filter((el): el is HTMLElement => el instanceof HTMLElement && el.offsetParent !== null)`. Risk: `offsetParent` is null for `position: fixed` elements, so if a future panel uses a fixed-position control prefer `el.checkVisibility()` with an offsetParent fallback.

plain.title: The shared focus trap assumes every match is a focusable element
plain.what: The focus trap collects elements by a text pattern and assumes each result can receive focus, without checking.
plain.whyItMatters: In one dialog the last match is a hidden file input, so pressing Tab escapes the dialog — the exact thing a focus trap exists to prevent.
plain.whatToDo: Filter the collected matches to real focusable elements instead of assuming, and exclude hidden inputs.

findings.title: useBookRoute returns a book and a summary as independent values, and every direct book-to-book navigation commits a render where the summary belongs to the previous book
findings.description: CONSTRUCTIBLE IMPOSSIBLE STATE: `summary.bookId !== book.id`. `book` is derived synchronously from the route param on every render (line 13, `books.find(c => c.id === id)`), while `summary` is a `useState` slot written asynchronously by the effect at line 21. React Router renders the same `BookDetailPage` element for `book/:id` at the same tree position, so a /book/A -> /book/B navigation re-renders rather than remounts and the `summary` state survives. That means at least one committed frame has `book = B` and `summary = SummaryOf(A)`. HOW IT IS REACHED: the DailyWisdomModal is mounted in AppShell above the Outlet, so it can fire while the user is already on /book/A; its `onReadMore` calls `navigate('/book/' + dailyBook.id)` (AppShell.tsx:213) — a direct book-to-book navigation. Browser Back/Forward between two book pages does the same. CONSUMERS THAT MISHANDLE IT: (1) BookDetail renders `book.title` and `book.author` from the new book alongside `summary.oneSentenceTakeaway` (line 452), `summary.summary` (461), `summary.keyInsights` (470) and `summary.actionableSteps` (490) from the old one — the reader sees book B's title over book A's content. (2) Worse, the pair is a write source, not just a render source: `BookDetail.handleMasterclassClick` (BookDetail.tsx:184-187) captures the current `summary` for the whole duration of a streaming `generateDetailedSummary` call, then calls `onSummaryUpdate({ ...summary, detailedSummary })`, which BookDetailPage.tsx:44-46 forwards to `saveSummary`. `saveSummary` resolves the target book by `bookRepo.get(summary.bookId)` (useLibrary.tsx:81) — so a deep dive started on A and landing after a navigation to B is written onto A's summary while the page shows B, and B's reader then opens on 'No content available.' The type system permits all of this because `Book` and `Summary` are two unrelated values in an untagged bag; nothing expresses that they must agree on an id. HONEST SCOPE: the guaranteed part of this is the render-frame mismatch (short, but committed and painted); the persistent write to the wrong record needs an in-flight deep dive across the navigation.
findings.suggestedPatch: Smallest first step: make the pair inseparable rather than adding a tag. Replace the two independent slots with one, keyed by the book it belongs to — `const [loaded, setLoaded] = useState<{ bookId: string; summary: Summary | undefined } | null>(null)` — set it as `setLoaded({ bookId: book.id, summary: s })` inside the effect, and return `summary: loaded?.bookId === book?.id ? loaded.summary : undefined`. That is a ~6-line change confined to useBookRoute.ts; both consumers already accept `Summary | undefined`, so BookDetail and EReader need no edit and will simply show their existing not-yet-summarised states for the mismatched frame instead of the wrong book's text. Add a cancellation guard in the same effect (`let cancelled = false` / `if (!cancelled) setLoaded(...)`, the pattern ProfileContext.tsx:28 already uses) so a late resolution cannot overwrite a newer book. Does NOT require touching every producer and consumer.

plain.title: Moving directly between two books briefly shows the previous book's summary
plain.what: The book and its summary are loaded by two different mechanisms, one immediate and one delayed. Navigating from one book to another swaps the book instantly while the summary lags behind.
plain.whyItMatters: There is a committed render in which one book's page displays another book's summary, insights and takeaway. It is brief but real, and every screen reading the pair assumes they belong together.
plain.whatToDo: Load the pair as a single value tagged with the book it belongs to, so a mismatched combination cannot be rendered.

findings.title: The only CSV fixture is a canonical Goodreads header, so the parser's silent-coercion path for foreign CSVs is untested
findings.description: The only CSV fixture in goodreadsImport.test.tsx (lines 9-13) is a canonical Goodreads header, so every test in that file (42, 63, 80, 99) exercises `parseGoodreadsCsv` only on input it was designed for. The uncovered branch is goodreads.ts:96 `cell(index)` returning '' when `columnOf` yields -1 (goodreads.ts:83): a CSV that has a `title` column but neither `author` nor `exclusive shelf` parses as a clean success — verified by execution on a StoryGraph/Calibre-shaped header (`Title,Authors,Read Status,Star Rating`), which produced rows with `author: 'Unknown'` (goodreads.ts:109), `status: 'Want to Read'` (goodreads.ts:75,110), `rating: 0` (goodreads.ts:111) and `skipped: 0`. The declared return type `GoodreadsRow[]` with `status: BookStatus` claims validated domain data the parser never validated. The sibling suite narrows but does not close the gap: goodreads.test.ts:66-70 covers a reduced 3-column header, :72-75 covers reordered columns and :77-80 covers the 'Unknown' author fallback via an empty cell — none covers a missing author/shelf COLUMN. Untested production behaviour: a Calibre/StoryGraph/LibraryThing export dumping thousands of books authored 'Unknown', all 'Want to Read', behind a preview that reports success (GoodreadsImport.tsx:84-91). This is the test-coverage face of F019, which carries the production defect.

11   '1,Atomic Habits,James Clear,5,read,="9780735211292",2026/02/01',

13 ].join('\n');
--- src/lib/goodreads.ts:96,109 ---
96     const cell = (index: number) => (index >= 0 ? (cells[index] ?? '').trim() : '');
109       author: cell(authorAt) || 'Unknown',
findings.verifierNote: The coverage gap is real and I reproduced the untested behaviour, but two things need correcting: the claim about the sibling test file, and the severity. VERIFIED: goodreadsImport.test.tsx:9-13 is exactly as quoted and is the only CSV literal in that file; all four tests (lines 42, 63, 80, 99) feed either that canonical fixture or hand-built row objects (101-106), never a foreign header. I ran `parseGoodreadsCsv` on a StoryGraph/Calibre-shaped header (`Title,Authors,Read Status,Star Rating`) and got `{rows: [{title:'Dune', author:'Unknown', status:'Want to Read', rating:0}, ...], skipped: 0}` — a clean-looking success, exactly the silent-coercion path described, via goodreads.ts:83 `header.indexOf(name)` -> -1, goodreads.ts:96 `cell(-1)` -> '', then 109/110/111. CORRECTION: 'no test in this file (or in lib/goodreads.test.ts's sibling scope) feeds a CSV with a Title column but no Author/Exclusive Shelf column' overstates the gap — goodreads.test.ts:66-70 does test a reduced 3-column header, :72-75 tests reordered columns, and :77-80 tests the 'Unknown' author fallback (via an empty cell, not a missing column). What is genuinely untested is the precise combination 'title present, author AND exclusive shelf both absent' that yields all-defaults with `skipped: 0`. AMENDED TO MEDIUM: this is a test-coverage gap, not a production defect at the cited file:line — the production defect is F019 (same root cause, same parser), already rated high. Rating the test gap high as well double-counts.
findings.reachability: Not a runtime path — it is missing coverage. The production behaviour it fails to pin down is F019's: a user picking a StoryGraph or Calibre export imports every row as author 'Unknown' / status 'Want to Read' / rating 0 behind a preview that reports it as success (GoodreadsImport.tsx:84-91).
findings.blastRadius: Two test files (goodreadsImport.test.tsx, goodreads.test.ts) covering one parser (`parseGoodreadsCsv`, goodreads.ts:78-118) with 2 production callers: GoodreadsImport.tsx:24 and both test suites. The uncovered branch is goodreads.ts:96 `index >= 0 ? ... : ''` for the author and shelf columns specifically.

plain.title: The only import test uses a perfect Goodreads header, so foreign spreadsheets are untested
plain.what: Every import test feeds the parser exactly the file layout it was designed for. No test uses a spreadsheet from a different service.
plain.whyItMatters: A file with unrecognised headings imports every row with placeholder author, status and rating instead of failing, and no test would catch that regression.
plain.whatToDo: Add a table-driven case with a foreign header row alongside the existing header tests.

findings.title: localStorage recommendation cache is cast to a concrete shape and rendered without validation
findings.description: `JSON.parse(cached) as { at: number; items: Recommendation[] }` is a pure assertion over external, persistent, user-writable storage. The value flows unchecked into `setRecommendations(parsed.items)` and then into RecommendationCarousel.tsx:79 `recommendations.map(...)` and `rec.title` / `rec.author` / `rec.description` / `rec.coverUrl`. The try/catch on line 39 only covers `JSON.parse`, i.e. syntax errors -- a syntactically valid but wrong-shaped value passes the assertion, and the resulting failure happens later during the carousel's render, outside the catch, so the self-healing `localStorage.removeItem` on line 40 never runs. Concrete failure: a stored `{"at":,"items":"abc"}` satisfies the `parsed.items?.length` truthiness test (string length 3) and then throws `TypeError: recommendations.map is not a function` from the error boundary -- on every load, permanently, because the poison stays in localStorage. Milder always-live version: entries missing `coverUrl` render `` (React drops the attribute, so `onError` and the placeholder fallback on line 94 may never fire) and entries missing `title` produce `key={undefined}`. Reachability: the app is the only writer today, but a shared origin makes localStorage non-exclusive -- the planned Phase 4 GitHub Pages demo puts BookSum on `.github.io`, one origin shared with every other Pages site under that account -- and any future change to `Recommendation` leaves 24h of stale-shaped caches that still pass the TTL check. Correct behaviour: validate the parsed object (array check plus per-item field check) and drop the cache when it fails, the way ProfileView.tsx:119 at least array-checks its import.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed at LibraryPage.tsx:35: `const parsed = JSON.parse(cached) as { at: number; items: Recommendation[] };` - a bare assertion over localStorage, with the try/catch at :34-41 covering only JSON.parse, so a syntactically valid but wrong-shaped value passes and the self-healing removeItem at :40 never runs. The value flows to setRecommendations(:37) -> RecommendationCarousel `recommendations.map` (:79) and `rec.coverUrl`/`rec.title`/`rec.author` (:91-104). Two refinements from tracing the producer. (a) The app itself cannot write a non-array `items`: recommend.ts:34-39 always returns the result of `.map`, and a non-array `data.recommendations` throws inside recommend.ts's own try and is converted by toAiError - so the `items:"abc"` crash needs a foreign same-origin writer, devtools, or a future `Recommendation` shape change leaving 24h of stale caches. (b) The field-level variant IS live today: recommend.ts:35-36 spreads model output verbatim (`...rec`), so a response missing `title` yields `key={undefined}` and a missing `description` renders blank, then gets cached. Worth adding: the TTL test at :36 is `Date.now() - parsed.at < RECS_TTL_MS`, which is also true for any FUTURE `at`, so a poisoned entry with a forward timestamp never expires. Medium is right - localStorage ingress, no app-writable crash path today.
findings.reachability: Every load of the default route with a cached entry. The crash variant needs an external writer or a post-refactor shape change; the field-drift variant only needs one malformed model response to have been cached by :74-77.
findings.blastRadius: 1 read site (LibraryPage.tsx:32-42) feeding 1 component (RecommendationCarousel, 4 field reads), on the app's default route.
findings.suggestedPatch: Guard next to the parse: `const isRec = (v: unknown): v is Recommendation => !!v && typeof v === 'object' && typeof (v as Recommendation).title === 'string' && typeof (v as Recommendation).author === 'string';` then `const age = Date.now() - parsed?.at; if (typeof parsed?.at === 'number' && age >= 0 && age < RECS_TTL_MS && Array.isArray(parsed.items) && parsed.items.every(isRec)) setRecommendations(parsed.items); else localStorage.removeItem(key);`. Risk: stricter validation drops existing caches once on upgrade, which is the intended behaviour.

plain.title: Cached recommendations are read back from browser storage and rendered without checking
plain.what: The recommendation cache is read from local storage and assumed to have the expected shape. Nothing verifies it before it is displayed.
plain.whyItMatters: Browser storage is writable by the user and survives upgrades, so a stale or edited entry renders directly into the carousel.
plain.whatToDo: Check the cached value's shape next to where it is read, and discard the cache when it does not match.

findings.title: LibraryPage renders the zero-books empty state during the initial load because it never reads `isLoading`
findings.description: Consumer-side manifestation of L09-F03, on the app's default route. Line 18 destructures only `{ books, addBook, getSummary }` -- `isLoading` is available on the same object and is simply not taken -- so `filteredBooks.length > 0 ? grid : emptyState` treats the loading `[]` as 'this user has no books'. App.tsx:12 gates on `useProfile().isLoading`, not on the library's, so `LibraryProvider` mounts with a settled profile while `books` is still `[]` and `isLoading` is still `true`. The first paint of `/` for a user with 500 imported books is therefore 'Your library is quiet' plus an 'Add Your First Book' button, for the duration of the IndexedDB open + index read. The same array also drives `categories` (line 65), so the topic filter row is empty in that window. This is only possible because the producer's type does not tag its states; the fix here is to consume the tag (render a skeleton while loading), and it disappears entirely once L09-F03 is fixed. Blast radius: the default route, every cold load.

findings.title: The isLoading flag is only ever waited through, never asserted, so the false empty state on cold load is invisible
findings.description: `LibraryApi = ReturnType<typeof useLibraryState>` (useLibrary.tsx:185) is an untagged bag: `books: Book[]` and `isLoading: boolean` are returned as independent fields (useLibrary.tsx:171-172), so `const { books } = useLibrary()` compiles cleanly while `books` is still the initial `[]` (useLibrary.tsx:19-20). Of the seven production call sites, only useBookRoute.ts:10 reads `isLoading` — LibraryPage.tsx:18, StatsPage.tsx:6, ProfilePage.tsx:9 and AppShell.tsx:27 destructure `{ books }` alone. Because App.tsx:12 gates only on the profile load before mounting `LibraryProvider` (App.tsx:32), LibraryPage mounts with an empty array and renders the 'Your library is quiet' empty state (LibraryPage.tsx:188 -> 194-216, heading at line 200) on every cold load until the IndexedDB read at useLibrary.tsx:32 resolves; StatsPage and ProfilePage show zeroes for the same window. The gap is invisible to the suite: both Probes render `isLoading ? 'loading' : count` (useLibrary.test.tsx:13, goodreadsImport.test.tsx:19) but both `renderLibrary` helpers immediately wait past the loading window (lines 26 and 32), and no test asserts `isLoading === true` or mounts a real consumer during it. A discriminated union — `{ status: 'loading' } | { status: 'ready'; books: Book[] }` — would turn those four call sites into compile errors. Impact is a transient empty-state flash rather than data loss, and the defect lives in production source (useLibrary.tsx:170-183 and its unguarded consumers) rather than in the test file this was originally filed against.
findings.verifierNote: Every factual claim verifies; the severity and the anchor file do not. Both Probes render `api.isLoading ? 'loading' : count` (useLibrary.test.tsx:13, goodreadsImport.test.tsx:19) and both `renderLibrary` helpers immediately wait past the loading window (useLibrary.test.tsx:26, goodreadsImport.test.tsx:32); a repo-wide grep confirms no test anywhere asserts `isLoading === true` for the library. Exactly 7 production `useLibrary()` call sites — AppShell.tsx:27, StatsPage.tsx:6, ProfilePage.tsx:9, LibraryPage.tsx:18, GoodreadsImport.tsx:13, BookDetailPage.tsx:13, useBookRoute.ts:10 — and only useBookRoute.ts:10,16 reads `isLoading`. The empty-state flash is real: App.tsx:12 gates on the PROFILE load only and then mounts `LibraryProvider` (App.tsx:32), so LibraryPage mounts with `books: []` and renders 'Your library is quiet' (LibraryPage.tsx:188 -> 194-216, heading at line 200) until the IndexedDB read in useLibrary.tsx:32 resolves. AMENDED TO MEDIUM: the consequence is a transient empty-state flash on cold load — no data loss, no crash, self-correcting within one IndexedDB round-trip. That is the spec's 'erodes confidence and refactor safety but isn't on a critical path'. Also, the finding is anchored to a test-file line; the defect lives in production source at useLibrary.tsx:170-183 (the untagged return) and its four unguarded consumers.

plain.title: Tests always wait for loading to finish, so the false 'empty library' flash is invisible

findings.title: saveSummary is called by zero tests and the one summary test never asserts the denormalised Book fields
findings.description: useLibrary.test.tsx has zero coverage of `saveSummary` (verified: no test file in src/ mentions it) and its one summary test (lines 84-103) asserts only the summaries-store round-trip, never the denormalised `Book.oneSentenceTakeaway`/`readingTimeMinutes` pair that types.ts:41-48 documents as an invariant. The discoverer's claimed production route through useLibrary.tsx:82-83 is dead: saveSummary is only ever reached from BookDetail.tsx:186 (the deep-dive save, gated at :183 on an existing summary), where `book.summaryId` already equals `summary.id`, and both real addBook callers set the takeaway (AddBookModal.tsx:72, LibraryPage.tsx:92). The invariant IS violated for real at src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:105-119, which persists `summaryId` (line 117) with no `oneSentenceTakeaway`, so every migrated legacy book renders 'Not summarised yet' at BookCard.tsx:89 while its summary sits in the summaries store — and migrate.test.ts:100 checks only that `summaryId` is truthy. Because `summaryId?`, `oneSentenceTakeaway?` and `readingTimeMinutes` are three independent fields on one untagged interface, the compiler certifies that write.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern half-confirmed, reachability claim wrong, but the underlying union claim is corroborated by a site the discoverer missed. VERIFIED: `grep -rn saveSummary src/ --include=*.test.*` returns ZERO hits, so saveSummary genuinely has no test. useLibrary.test.tsx:84-103 asserts only the summaries-store read (line 101) and `record.summaryId` (line 102); the `draft()` fixture at lines 30-39 hard-codes `readingTimeMinutes: 12` (line 36) and omits `oneSentenceTakeaway`, legal per types.ts:48. REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: 'saveSummary is the function BookDetailPage.tsx:46 actually calls when an AI summary is generated' is false. Its only caller chain is BookDetail.tsx:186 `onSummaryUpdate(updated)` inside `handleMasterclassClick`, which returns early at BookDetail.tsx:183 `if (!summary) return;` — it is the deep-dive detailedSummary save, where `book.summaryId === summary.id` already holds, so the guard at useLibrary.tsx:82 `if (book && book.summaryId !== summary.id)` is false and the claimed impossible-state write at line 83 never fires. CORROBORATION the discoverer missed: src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:105-119 calls `books.create({...})` with `summaryId` (line 117) and `readingTimeMinutes` (line 115) but NO `oneSentenceTakeaway` key at all, while summaries.upsert at 122-132 writes the real takeaway to the summaries store. findings.title: useLibrary returns an untagged `{ books, isLoading }` bag, so `Book[]` cannot distinguish 'empty' from 'not loaded yet'
findings.description: useLibrary returns `books: Book[]` and `isLoading: boolean` as independent fields (useLibrary.tsx:170-182), so nothing in the type stops a consumer from treating the initial `[]` (useLibrary.tsx:19) as an authoritative empty library while the read at line 32 is still in flight. Of 7 consumers, only useBookRoute.ts:10 takes `isLoading`, and it needs it (line 16 guards the redirect at line 18); AppShell.tsx:27, LibraryPage.tsx:18, ProfilePage.tsx:9 and StatsPage.tsx:6 read `books` alone and the compiler cannot flag them. The reachable consequence is a flash of the wrong state on first paint — LibraryPage.tsx:194-216 shows 'Your library is quiet' and StatsPage.tsx:9 shows zeroes for the duration of one IndexedDB round-trip. The finding's sharper claim that ProfilePage.tsx:24's 'Delete everything' would delete a stale subset is not reachable: it is gated behind the async confirm at ProfilePage.tsx:16-22, which cannot be accepted inside that window. The profile gate itself is correct (useLibrary.tsx:25, App.tsx:12/22).

plain.title: The library hook cannot distinguish 'no books' from 'not loaded yet'
plain.what: The library returns a list of books and a separate loading flag as two unrelated values, so an empty list looks authoritative even before anything has been read.
plain.whyItMatters: Four of the six screens that use it ignore the flag, producing a false empty state on every cold load and skewing what is shown on the statistics page.
plain.whatToDo: Give the pages that render an empty list a loading branch first, then consider returning one tagged value instead of two independent ones.

findings.title: The feature's entire public contract is inferred: `LibraryApi = ReturnType<typeof useLibraryState>`
findings.description: `useLibraryState` is module-private and carries no return type annotation; `LibraryApi` is derived from it with `ReturnType<>`, and `useLibrary(): LibraryApi` therefore has an annotation that is just an alias for 'whatever the implementation currently happens to return'. Nothing declares what this module promises. An incidental change inside any of the ten `useCallback`s -- a widened parameter, a narrowed return, a renamed key in the returned object literal -- silently rewrites the feature's public API, and TypeScript reports the breakage at the six consumer sites rather than at the source. There is no interface to diff a PR against and no place to document the contract. The repo already has the idiomatic fix one folder over: src/features/profile/ProfileContext.tsx:9-18 declares `interface ProfileContextValue` explicitly and annotates `useProfile(): ProfileContextValue`. `LibraryProvider` (line 193) likewise has no return annotation. Blast radius: six app call sites (AppShell.tsx:27, LibraryPage.tsx:18, StatsPage.tsx:6, ProfilePage.tsx:9, BookDetailPage.tsx:13, useBookRoute.ts:10, GoodreadsImport.tsx:13) plus two test files that re-derive `ReturnType<typeof useLibrary>`.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed exactly: useLibrary.tsx:17 `function useLibraryState()` carries no return annotation, :185 is `export type LibraryApi = ReturnType<typeof useLibraryState>;`, and :198 `export function useLibrary(): LibraryApi` is an annotation that resolves to 'whatever the implementation returns today'. The returned literal at :170-182 has 11 members, all inferred. The contrast the finding draws is real: ProfileContext.tsx:9-18 declares `interface ProfileContextValue` explicitly and annotates `useProfile(): ProfileContextValue` at :111. Blast radius recount: 7 non-test consumers, not six - AppShell.tsx:27, BookDetailPage.tsx:13, useBookRoute.ts:10, GoodreadsImport.tsx:13, LibraryPage.tsx:18, ProfilePage.tsx:9, StatsPage.tsx:6 - plus test files re-deriving `ReturnType<typeof useLibrary>` (goodreadsImport.test.tsx:15). The sub-claim about LibraryProvider (:193) lacking a return annotation is weak and I would not act on it: inferring the element type of a React component is idiomatic. Medium holds - pure refactor-safety erosion, no runtime consequence.
findings.reachability: No runtime path. Manifests on change: a narrowed return or renamed key inside any of the 11 members reports at the 7 consumers instead of at the source, with no interface to diff a PR against.
findings.blastRadius: 7 non-test call sites plus test files; 11 exported members.
findings.suggestedPatch: Declare the contract and annotate the implementation: `export interface LibraryApi { books: Book[]; isLoading: boolean; addBook(draft: BookDraft, options?: AddBookOptions): Promise<Book>; updateBook(book: Book): Promise<void>; removeBook(id: string): Promise<void>; getSummary(bookId: string): Promise<Summary | undefined>; saveSummary(summary: Summary): Promise<void>; exportLibrary(): Promise<LibraryExport>; importLibrary(payload: LibraryExport): Promise<number>; importGoodreadsRows(rows: GoodreadsRow[]): Promise<{ added: number; duplicates: number }>; reload(): Promise<void>; }` then `function useLibraryState(): LibraryApi`. Risk: the explicit interface surfaces any place the inferred type was accidentally wider than intended - the point of the change, but it may need one or two call-site fixes.

plain.title: The library feature has no written contract; its public shape is whatever the code happens to return
plain.what: The library's public interface is derived automatically from the implementation rather than declared, so the implementation cannot disagree with it.
plain.whyItMatters: Any accidental change to a returned value silently becomes the new contract, and consumers only find out at runtime.
plain.whatToDo: Declare the interface explicitly and annotate the implementation against it.

findings.title: addBook is the one site that mints a summary id and a book id together, and swapping them type-checks and leaves no runtime trace
findings.description: COMPILING-WRONG-CALL: `Summary.id` and `Summary.bookId` are both bare `string` (types.ts:55-56) and `Book.id` is bare `string` (types.ts:29). At useLibrary.tsx:48 both values are in scope at once, so writing `await summaryRepo.upsert({ ...options.summary, id: book.id, bookId: summaryId })` — the two identifiers transposed — satisfies `Summary` exactly and `npx tsc --noEmit` stays at exit 0. WHY IT IS UNDETECTABLE AT RUNTIME TOO: every id in the system comes from `crypto.randomUUID()` (repo.ts:4 `newId`, useLibrary.tsx:44, srs.ts:24, toastStore.ts:17), so both values are indistinguishable v4 UUIDs — no length check, no prefix, no assertion, and no IndexedDB constraint can catch the swap. CONSUMER THAT MISHANDLES IT: `summaries.getByBook(bookId)` (repo.ts:112) reads the `by-book` index, so it would return `undefined` for the book forever, while `Book.summaryId` still points at a stored record — which is precisely the 'summarised but no summary' contradiction F050/F011/F012 already document as a visible UI failure, arriving here as silent write-time corruption instead. `books.remove` (repo.ts:68-70) resolves the orphan via `getByBook` too, so it would never delete it. CORROBORATION THAT THIS CONFUSION IS ALREADY LIVE: ProfileView.tsx:88 builds `const summaryById = new Map(data.summaries.map((s) => [s.bookId, s]))` — a map named 'ById' that is keyed by *book* id. Correcting the map to match its own name compiles (both fields are `string`) and makes `summaryById.get(b.id)` return `undefined` for every book, at which point `libraryToMarkdown` silently writes 'Not summarised yet.' (markdown.ts:19-20) for the entire library export with no error. HONEST SCOPE: no call site is wrong today; this is a latent foot-gun, and it is reported because the failure mode is silent, unrecoverable data corruption with zero runtime signal — the exact profile the spec says branded types are worth paying for.
findings.suggestedPatch: Smallest first step that pays off, and it is genuinely small because the ids have exactly one producer: in src/lib/storage/repo.ts add `export type BookId = string & { readonly __brand: 'BookId' }` and `SummaryId`, retype `newId` to a generic `const newId = <T extends string>() => crypto.randomUUID() as T`, and brand only the three fields that actually collide — `Book.id: BookId`, `Summary.id: SummaryId`, `Summary.bookId: BookId`. HONEST RETROFIT COST: branding `Book.id` alone touches every producer and consumer of a book id (useLibrary, useBookRoute, BookDetail/BookDetailPage, QuizModal, blobs.*, reviewCards.*, migrate.ts, the LibraryExport round-trip and the repo tests) and will need `as BookId` at the two boundaries where ids come back from JSON (`importLibrary`) and from the route param (`useParams`). If that is too much, the strictly-cheaper 90% fix is to stop having the two values in scope together: change `AddBookOptions.summary` to be written by a single repo helper `summaries.createFor(book, draft)` that mints the id itself, so useLibrary never holds both a summary id and a book id at the same time. That is a ~10-line change in one file and removes the swap opportunity outright.

plain.title: One place creates a book identifier and a summary identifier together, and swapping them would go unnoticed
plain.what: All record identifiers are plain text. In the routine that adds a book, both a new book identifier and a new summary identifier are in scope at once and are interchangeable to the compiler.
plain.whyItMatters: Transposing them compiles cleanly, writes successfully, and leaves no error. The summary would simply never be found again, showing as 'no summary yet' forever.
plain.whatToDo: Give the two identifier kinds distinct types at the single place they are created, which keeps the change small.

plain.what: A test button reaches for the first profile and overrides the compiler's warning that there might not be one. Two tests in the same file run with no profiles at all.

findings.title: ProfileContextValue models loading and profile as independent fields, so the type permits acting on a null profile mid-load
findings.description:
`ProfileContextValue` exposes `profile: Profile | null` and `isLoading: boolean` as orthogonal fields. The three states that actually exist — loading (profile not yet known), settled-with-profile, settled-without-profile — are encoded as four representable combinations, and the compiler cannot tell them apart. `profile === null` is ambiguous between 'still loading' and 'no profile selected', which is exactly the failure CLAUDE.md records as learned the hard way: 'Hooks that depend on the profile must wait for useProfile().isLoading to settle, or they will act on a null profile and silently drop the write.' The type does not enforce that rule; it is documentation only, which is why `useLibrary.tsx:25` and `useReviewQueue.ts:14` each hand-roll the same `if (profileLoading) return;` line with a comment explaining why.

Blast radius: 10 non-test consumers of `useProfile()`. Only 3 read `isLoading` (`App.tsx:10`, `useLibrary.tsx:18`, `useReviewQueue.ts:9`). The other 7 — `useTheme.ts:15`, `AppShell.tsx:26`, `ProfilePage.tsx:8`, `ProfilePicker.tsx:7`, `LibraryPage.tsx:17`, `BookDetailPage.tsx:14`, `ReaderPage.tsx:10` — destructure `profile` and treat `null` as 'no profile', with the type raising no objection.

Honest scoping: there is no live bug, because `App.tsx:12-18` gates the entire tree on `isLoading` before rendering anything, so no consumer in this lot can observe the loading state. That single gate is the only thing making the other 7 consumers correct, and it is invisible to the type system. Move it, add a route outside it, or render any of these components in a test/Storybook harness without the gate, and the silent-drop class returns with no compiler error — e.g. `useTheme.setTheme` (useTheme.ts:33-39) returns `Promise<void>` that resolves as if the write succeeded while `if (!profile) return;` discards it.

Correct behavior: a tagged union (`{ status: 'loading' } | { status: 'ready'; profile: Profile } | { status: 'no-profile' }`) so `profile` is only reachable after narrowing, making the gate compiler-enforced instead of convention-enforced. Verified negatives in this file: `createContext<ProfileContextValue | undefined>(undefined)` (line 20) is honest — no `null as unknown as T` default — and `useProfile()` throws outside the provider (line 113) and annotates its return explicitly.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed and, unusually, honestly self-scoped by the discovery agent. ProfileContext.tsx:9-18 declares `profile: Profile | null` (:10) and `isLoading: boolean` (:12) as orthogonal fields, so the three real states are encoded as four representable combinations and `profile === null` is ambiguous between 'still loading' and 'no profile'. My recount matches the finding exactly: 10 non-test `useProfile()` consumers (App.tsx:10, AppShell.tsx:26, BookDetailPage.tsx:14, ReaderPage.tsx:10, LibraryPage.tsx:17, useLibrary.tsx:18, ProfilePage.tsx:8, ProfilePicker.tsx:7, useReviewQueue.ts:9, useTheme.ts:15), of which exactly 3 read `isLoading` (App.tsx:10, useLibrary.tsx:18, useReviewQueue.ts:9). The finding's own caveat is correct: App.tsx:12-18 gates the whole tree, so there is no live bug, and useLibrary.tsx:25 / useReviewQueue.ts:14 hand-roll `if (profileLoading) return;` with comments explaining why. The foot-gun cost is demonstrably real rather than hypothetical - CLAUDE.md records this exact class ('act on a null profile and silently drop the write') as learned the hard way, and useTheme.ts:15 does NOT take isLoading while useTheme.ts:33-39 returns a `Promise<void>` that resolves as though the write succeeded. That is what keeps it at medium rather than low despite there being no current incident path.
findings.reachability: No live path: App.tsx:12 renders a spinner until the profile settles, and LibraryProvider/AppRoutes mount only after. Returns the moment a route is added outside that gate, the gate moves, or any of these components is rendered in a harness without it - e.g. `useTheme.setTheme` (useTheme.ts:33-39) silently discards the write via `if (!profile) return;` and still resolves.
findings.blastRadius: 10 non-test consumers; 7 of them destructure `profile` and treat null as 'no profile' with no compiler objection.
findings.suggestedPatch: Expose a tagged state alongside (not instead of) the current fields to keep the migration incremental: `type ProfileState = { status: 'loading' } | { status: 'ready'; profile: Profile } | { status: 'no-profile' }`, add `state: ProfileState` to ProfileContextValue, migrate consumers one at a time, then drop `profile`/`isLoading`. Risk: a big-bang switch touches all 10 consumers at once; the additive form lets typecheck stay green between steps.

plain.title: The profile context lets code act on a missing profile while loading is still in progress
plain.what: The profile and the loading flag are exposed as two unrelated values, so the three real states are encoded as four possible combinations.
plain.whyItMatters: The project has already recorded that acting on a not-yet-loaded profile silently drops writes. The type permits exactly that mistake.
plain.whatToDo: Expose a tagged state alongside the existing fields so consumers can be migrated gradually.

findings.title: The suite's only options: [] card is built to be cascade-deleted, never mounted in the queue
findings.description: reviewQueue.test.tsx's shared `seedCard` helper (lines 17-27) always builds `options: ['a','b','c','d']` (line 22), and the file's only empty-options card (line 149) sits inside the cascade-delete test at 131-158, which never calls `mount()` — so no test in the suite ever mounts the unanswerable state, even though `ReviewCard.options: string[]` (types.ts:88) and `newCard` (srs.ts:28) both accept it without complaint. The production consequence is the deadlock already filed as F024 (ReviewPage.tsx:93/75/125). This finding's independent contribution is the missing regression test, and the right structural fix is runtime validation at the AI/queue boundary or a non-empty tuple type — not a discriminated union, since `options` carries no tag to narrow on.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern confirmed at its current lines, but this is the test-side mirror of F024 and the category is wrong. VERIFIED: the shared helper `seedCard` at reviewQueue.test.tsx:17-27 always builds `options: ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']` (line 22), so every card that reaches the queue in this suite is well-formed. The file's only `options: []` is line 149, inside the 'drops a book cards when the book is deleted' test at lines 131-158 — and that test never calls `mount()` (compare lines 53, 63, 74, 84, 103, 120 which all do), so the card is created at 144-153 and immediately cascade-deleted at 155, asserted at 157. It is never `current`, never rendered, never graded. The deadlock consequence the finding describes is correct and I verified it independently (see F024): ReviewPage.tsx:93/75/125-134, useReviewQueue.ts:38-39, repo.ts:89 sorting ascending. srs.ts:22-36 `newCard` copies `options` through with no non-empty check (line 28), so `newCard({ options: [] })` type-checks — that part of the claim is real. AMENDED on two counts. (1) Category: `options: string[]` is not a union and there is no tag field to narrow on, so `discriminated-union-opportunity` does not fit the spec's definition; the fix is runtime validation at the AI/queue boundary (or a non-empty tuple), which is `boundary-without-validation`. (2) Severity: the production defect is already filed at high as F024 (and its root cause at critical as F005). F025's independent contribution is 'no test mounts an empty-options card', a coverage gap — medium.
findings.reachability: Same production path as F024 (quiz generation -> persisted card -> /review deadlock). The test-file finding itself is not user-reachable; its value is that reviewQueue.test.tsx:144-153 compiling proves the type admits the state, while nothing in the suite renders it.
findings.blastRadius: Test-only as filed: 1 fixture (reviewQueue.test.tsx:144-153) in a 7-test suite; the shared seedCard at lines 17-27 covers the other 6. Underlying production blast radius is F024's.

plain.title: The one test card with no answer options is built only to be deleted, never to be reviewed
plain.what: Every card the review tests create has a full set of options. The single card without them exists inside a deletion test that never opens the queue.

findings.title: useReviewQueue has no return annotation, so `current` is inferred as a definite ReviewCard while the runtime returns undefined
findings.description:
`useReviewQueue` is exported with no explicit return type, so its contract is whatever TypeScript infers from the returned object literal. With `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` off (tsconfig.json sets only `strict: true`), `queue[0]` infers as `ReviewCard`, not `ReviewCard | undefined`. The hook's public type therefore states that `current` is always a card — which is false for the overwhelmingly common case of an empty queue (nothing due), and false on first paint before `reload()` resolves.

No crash today: `ReviewPage.tsx:52` guards with `if (!current)` and renders the 'Nothing due' state, and `useReviewQueue.ts:36-37` guards internally with `const [current] = queue; if (!current) return;`. Both guards are correct — and both are, as far as the compiler is concerned, dead code testing a value that can never be falsy. That is the actual danger: the type actively argues against the only thing keeping the feature alive. A second consumer (a nav badge doing `current.question.slice(0, 40)`, a keyboard-shortcut handler, a test helper) gets zero compiler pressure to guard and throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`. Equally, enabling `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` — not currently configured in eslint.config.js, which runs untyped rules only — would report both existing guards as removable, inviting a 'cleanup' that turns the empty-queue path into a hard crash on the Review page.

Correct behavior: annotate the hook's return with `current: ReviewCard | undefined` (or enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) so the guard is required rather than tolerated. Blast radius: currently one consumer (`ReviewPage`), so this is refactor-safety rather than a live defect; the fix is trivial and makes both existing guards provably load-bearing.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed on all counts. useReviewQueue.ts:8 `export function useReviewQueue()` has no return annotation; :44-51 returns an object literal whose `current: queue[0]` (:46) infers as `ReviewCard` because tsconfig.json (read directly) sets only `strict: true` - no noUncheckedIndexedAccess - so the hook's public type claims a card always exists, which is false for the empty queue that ends every session and for the first paint before reload() resolves. Both guards the finding names are present and, per the declared types, provably dead: useReviewQueue.ts:35-36 `const [current] = queue; if (!current) return;` and ReviewPage.tsx:52 `if (!current)`. The eslint claim checks out too: eslint.config.js has no type-aware setup (no projectService/parserOptions project reference and no `no-unnecessary-condition`), so nothing flags them today - but enabling typed linting would report both as removable and invite a 'cleanup' that turns the empty-queue path into a hard crash. Blast radius as claimed: exactly 1 non-test consumer (ReviewPage.tsx:37). Medium is right - refactor safety, not a live defect.
findings.reachability: No crash today; ReviewPage.tsx:52 guards. The type invites a crash in any second consumer (a nav 'due' badge, a keyboard shortcut, a test helper) that trusts `current` and skips the guard - the compiler applies zero pressure.
findings.blastRadius: 1 non-test consumer (ReviewPage.tsx:37) plus the test probe; 6 returned members.
findings.suggestedPatch: `export interface ReviewQueueApi { queue: ReviewCard[]; current: ReviewCard | undefined; remaining: number; isLoading: boolean; grade: (grade: Grade) => Promise<void>; reload: () => Promise<void>; }` then `export function useReviewQueue(): ReviewQueueApi`. Risk: none - ReviewPage.tsx:52 already guards, so the annotation compiles as-is and simply makes that guard load-bearing. (Enabling noUncheckedIndexedAccess project-wide would fix this too but is a much larger change - prefer the annotation.)

plain.title: The review queue reports a definite current card when there may be none
plain.what: The review queue's public shape is inferred rather than declared, and the inference says the current card always exists because a compiler option that would say otherwise is switched off.
plain.whyItMatters: Every consumer is told the card is present. The runtime returns nothing once the queue is empty, so the guard the compiler considers unnecessary is the only thing preventing a crash.
plain.whatToDo: Declare the interface explicitly with the current card marked as possibly absent.

findings.title: src/lib/ai ships 11 modules and 2 test files; every JSON.parse-as-T boundary is in the untested nine
findings.description: src/lib/ai ships 11 modules but only 2 test files (apiKey.test.ts, which also exercises client.ts, and errors.test.ts) — verified by directory listing. All four `JSON.parse(response.text || '{}') as T` sites live in the untested nine (summarize.ts:52, summarize.ts:73, recommend.ts:30, quiz.ts:16) and none has a runtime guard; the `responseSchema` passed to Gemini is a request hint, and the `??`/`||` coalescing at summarize.ts:28-37 only rescues nullish values, never a wrong type. This is a coverage statistic over ingress points that are already enumerated individually as F005 (quiz.ts:16), F030 (recommend.ts:30), F033 (summarize.ts:36) and F034 (summarize.ts:52) — it adds the observation that no test would ever notice when the runtime disagrees with the assertion, not a new defect.
findings.verifierNote: Every count and citation is factually correct, but this is a rollup of defects already filed individually at higher severity in the same aggregate. VERIFIED by `ls src/lib/ai/`: exactly 11 non-test modules (apiKey, chat, client, errors, models, prompts, quiz, recommend, schemas, summarize, tts) and exactly 2 test files (apiKey.test.ts, errors.test.ts). apiKey.test.ts:1-11 imports from './apiKey', './client' and './errors' — confirming the three-module coverage claim. VERIFIED by `grep -rn 'JSON.parse' src/lib/ai/`: exactly four parse sites, all in untested modules — summarize.ts:52 and summarize.ts:73 (`as RawBookResponse`), recommend.ts:30 (`as { recommendations?: ... }`), quiz.ts:16 (`as { questions?: QuizQuestion[] }`). The coalescing claim is correct: summarize.ts:28-37 uses `data.rating ?? 0`, `data.keyInsights ?? []`, `data.oneSentenceTakeaway || 'No takeaway available.'` — nullish/falsy guards that cannot rescue a wrong runtime type. quiz.ts:17 `return data.questions ?? []` confirmed, and correctAnswerIndex is unbounded against options.length (schemas.ts:69-72 states the bound only in a prose `description`). AMENDED DOWN for two reasons the spec's own author notes support ('Discovery is necessary but not sufficient... lead with WHICH any matters'): (a) all four constituent boundaries are already filed separately and at equal-or-higher severity in this aggregate — F005 (quiz.ts:16, critical), F030 (recommend.ts:30, high), F033 (summarize.ts:36, high), F034 (summarize.ts:52, high) — so counting this at high triple-counts the same ingress; (b) the finding is anchored at apiKey.test.ts:1, a file with no relationship to the claim, and its own text concedes it is 'a risk multiplier rather than a standalone defect'. Its residual, non-duplicative value is the coverage statistic, which is medium.
findings.reachability: Not a defect with a user path of its own — it is the absence of tests over the four Gemini-response parse sites. Each individual reachable failure is described by F005/F030/F033/F034.

plain.title: Nine of the eleven AI modules have no tests at all, including every place AI output is trusted
plain.what: The AI folder ships eleven modules and two test files. Every point where a model reply is converted into app data sits in the untested nine.
