findings.title: sendMessageStream returns `Promise<string>` that is silently empty on a blocked completion, leaving a permanently blank chat bubble
findings.description: `chunk.text` is `string | undefined` in the SDK (genai.d.ts:9465) and line 33 coalesces it to `''`. If the model produces no text at all — a safety block on the reply, an immediately-truncated stream, or an empty candidate list — the loop completes without throwing and the function returns `''`. The return type `Promise<string>` cannot express that difference, so callers have no compiler-visible reason to handle it. ChatModal.tsx:59 pushes a placeholder `{ role: 'model', text: '' }` before the call, `onChunk` is never invoked so the placeholder is never filled, and the recovery code at ChatModal.tsx:70-79 lives in a `catch` that never fires. The user sees an empty assistant bubble that stays empty, with no error toast and no retry affordance. The catch block is even written to replace a model message whose `text === ''` (line 75) — the exact state produced here — so the intended handling exists but is unreachable on this path. Correct shape: throw an `AiError` (errors.ts already defines the `'safety'` kind and its copy at errors.ts:33) when the accumulated text is empty, or return a tagged result the caller must destructure. Blast radius: 1 call site (ChatModal.tsx:61).
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed end to end. chat.ts:32 coalesces `chunk.text ?? ''` and :35 returns the accumulated string, so a completion that yields no text at all (safety block on the reply, empty candidate list, immediately-truncated stream) completes the loop without throwing and returns `''`; `Promise<string>` at :27 cannot express the difference, so callers get no compiler-visible reason to handle it. On the consumer side ChatModal.tsx:59 pushes the placeholder `{ role: 'model', text: '' }`, :61 awaits the stream, `onChunk` is never invoked so the placeholder is never filled, and the recovery block at :69-79 is inside a `catch` that never fires on this path - while the condition it uses, `entry.text === ''` at :74, describes exactly the state produced here. The user is left with a permanently blank assistant bubble, no toast, no retry affordance. The suggested shape is supported: errors.ts:1-9 already defines the `'safety'` kind and errors.ts:33 its user-facing copy. Medium is right - one call site, UI dead-end, no crash or data loss.
findings.reachability: Ask a question in the book chat that Gemini declines to answer (safety/recitation finish reason with no text parts): the assistant bubble appears and stays empty forever.
findings.blastRadius: 1 call site (ChatModal.tsx:61). `createBookChatSession` is unaffected.
findings.suggestedPatch: chat.ts:35 -> `if (text === '') throw new AiError('safety', MESSAGES-backed copy); return text;` - concretely `if (!text) throw new AiError('safety', 'Gemini blocked this request under its safety filters. Try a different book or wording.');` (import AiError from './errors'). ChatModal's existing catch at :69-79 then fills the empty placeholder with the message, so no consumer change is needed. Risk: a legitimate empty reply (model chooses silence) would now surface as an error - acceptable, since a blank bubble is not a usable outcome either.

plain.title: A blocked chat reply arrives as an empty message bubble with no explanation
plain.what: The chat stream converts a missing reply into an empty string, and an empty string is indistinguishable from a valid one at the point it is used.
plain.whyItMatters: A blocked or truncated answer renders as a permanently blank bubble; the user has no idea whether to wait, retry, or rephrase.
plain.whatToDo: Treat an entirely empty stream as a failure so the existing error handling can report it.

findings.title: apiError fixture defaults its message to 'boom', so the 403 -> invalid-key assertion proves nothing
findings.description: errors.test.ts:4-6 defaults its `apiError` fixture message to the literal 'boom', which matches none of the substring branches at errors.ts:53-54, so the it.each table at lines 14-23 exercises the status switch at errors.ts:58-61 in isolation. That is a valid unit test as far as it goes — and lines 25-27 and 29-31 deliberately pin the message-beats-status precedence, so the precedence is documented intent, not a bug the fixture conceals. What the fixture does hide is that it models ApiError's shape but never its content: per node_modules/@google/genai/dist/web/index.mjs:14249-14254 the SDK's `message` is `JSON.stringify(errorBody)` — the whole error document — so any 4xx body containing 'blocked' or 'quota' anywhere is misclassified before the typed `status` is read, and no test in this file would notice. This is the test-side sibling of the production defect filed as F029.
findings.verifierNote: Fixture and mechanism confirmed; the headline claim overshoots and the finding duplicates F029's test observation. VERIFIED: errors.test.ts:4-6 `function apiError(status: number, message = 'boom') { return Object.assign(new Error(message), { name: 'ApiError', status }); }`; the it.each table at lines 14-23 with `[403, 'invalid-key']` at line 17 and the assertion at line 22. VERIFIED precedence in errors.ts:53-61 — `lower.includes('quota')` at 53, then `lower.includes('safety') || lower.includes('blocked')` at 54, and only in the trailing `else` at 57-61 does `statusOf(error)` run. So 'boom' (which contains none of those substrings and is neither a SyntaxError nor a TypeError) does fall through to the status switch — the discoverer's mechanism is right. REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: 'the 403 -> invalid-key assertion proves nothing.' It proves the status branch maps correctly for a message with no trigger substring, which is a real (if narrow) unit. More importantly, errors.test.ts:25-27 ('detects a quota message ahead of the raw status', asserting `apiError(429, 'Quota exceeded...')` -> 'quota') and errors.test.ts:29-31 ('maps a safety block', asserting `apiError(400, 'Response blocked due to SAFETY')` -> 'safety') show the message-before-status precedence is deliberate and explicitly covered — it is not something the 'boom' fixture is concealing. WHAT SURVIVES, and is real: no test in the file ever passes a realistic SDK message. Per node_modules/@google/genai/dist/web/index.mjs:14249-14254 the SDK sets `message` to `JSON.stringify(errorBody)` — the entire error document — so any 4xx whose body contains the substring 'blocked' or 'quota' anywhere (field names and nested details included) is misclassified, and this fixture models ApiError's SHAPE but not its CONTENT, so the suite cannot detect it. NOT REPO-VERIFIABLE: the specific wording 'Requests from referer <empty> are blocked.' is external knowledge; I could not confirm it from this repo, only the mechanism. Amended to medium: this is the test-side sibling of F029 (which I confirmed at high), and its own headline is overstated.
findings.reachability: The test defect itself is not user-reachable. The production misclassification it fails to catch is F029's: any Gemini 4xx whose JSON body contains 'blocked' or 'quota' is tagged 'safety'/'quota' before errors.ts:58-61 ever reads the typed `status`.
findings.blastRadius: One test file (errors.test.ts, 7 tests) over one function; that function has 16 direct call sites (verified by grep: 9 in src/lib/ai, 7 in UI) plus 3 via handleAiError.

plain.title: The AI error tests use a placeholder message, so they pass without proving anything
plain.what: Every test error is built with the message 'boom', which matches none of the classification rules being tested. The tests therefore exercise a path the real service never produces.
plain.whyItMatters: The misclassification that leaves users unable to reach the key dialog ships with a fully green test suite that appears to cover it. This is the clearest example in the audit of a test that proves nothing.
plain.whatToDo: Make the fixture reproduce the real message shape the service sends, then add the case that fails today.

findings.title: No fixture passes a non-object to toAiError(error: unknown), which throws on null/undefined via an unguarded as-cast
findings.description:
Every fixture in this file constructs a real `Error`: `apiError()` on lines 4-6, `new MissingKeyError()`, `new TypeError(...)`, `new SyntaxError(...)`. Nothing ever passes `null`, `undefined`, a bare string or a number — the values `toAiError(error: unknown)` explicitly declares it accepts.

`errors.ts:39-42` does `const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status;` with no null guard. For `undefined` the flow is: `message = String(undefined)` -> `'undefined'`, which contains none of `quota`/`safety`/`blocked`; not a `SyntaxError`; not a `TypeError`; so it falls to the `else` on line 57 and dereferences `.status` on `undefined` -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')`. Same for `null`.

`toAiError` is the app's universal error normaliser — every AI entry point wraps its body in `catch (error) { throw toAiError(error) }` (`summarize.ts:56/77/101`, `quiz.ts:19`, and the rest). A function whose entire job is to turn ANYTHING into a friendly `AiError` instead throws a raw `TypeError` for two of the values its own parameter type admits, so instead of a toast the user gets an unhandled rejection. `Promise.reject()` with no argument and `throw undefined` from third-party code both reach it. The `as { status?: unknown }` is the lie: it claims the value is an object.

What goes untested: the non-object branch of a function typed to accept `unknown`.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed, and I traced the throw by hand against the current source. errors.ts:39-42 `statusOf` does `const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status;` with no null guard, and toAiError(undefined) flows: :46 not an AiError -> :48 `message = String(undefined)` = 'undefined' -> :53/:54 no 'quota'/'safety'/'blocked' match -> :55 not SyntaxError -> :56 not TypeError -> :57 else -> :58 `statusOf(undefined)` -> :40 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')`. Identical for null. Strings and numbers are safe (property access boxes the primitive), so it is exactly the two nullish values that break. errors.test.ts contains no such fixture: :4-6 `apiError` builds a real Error, and every other case is `new MissingKeyError()` / `new TypeError` (:34) / `new SyntaxError` (:38) / apiError (:14-23, :25-31, :41-47). The `as { status?: unknown }` is the lie - it asserts objecthood on a parameter declared `unknown`. This is a genuine bug in the app's universal error normaliser (every AI entry point does `catch (error) { throw toAiError(error) }`), so it belongs in the report's 'Bugs discovered' section. Medium is right: the fix is one line, but the triggering values (`throw undefined`, `Promise.reject()` with no argument) are rare in practice, so I would not raise it to high without a demonstrated producer.
findings.reachability: Requires an upstream `throw undefined` / `throw null` / `Promise.reject()` inside one of the wrapped try blocks (summarize.ts:56/77/101, quiz.ts:19, chat.ts:18/37, recommend.ts:41). I could not find a producer in the SDK or app code, so the crash is latent - but the function's declared parameter type promises to handle it.
findings.blastRadius: 1 function, called from every AI entry point (6+ catch sites). A throw here replaces a toast with an unhandled rejection.
findings.suggestedPatch: errors.ts:39-42 -> `function statusOf(error: unknown): number | undefined { if (typeof error !== 'object' || error === null) return undefined; const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status; return typeof status === 'number' ? status : undefined; }` and add two table cases to errors.test.ts: `it.each([[undefined], [null], ['boom'], [42]])('normalises %p to an AiError', (v) => expect(toAiError(v)).toBeInstanceOf(AiError))`. Risk: none - strictly widens the accepted input set.

plain.title: No error test ever passes something that is not an error object
plain.what: Every failure fixture in the error tests builds a real error. The empty and non-object cases, which are the ones that throw, are never tried.
plain.whyItMatters: The classification routine's only genuine crash is in a case the tests structurally cannot reach.
plain.whatToDo: Add the guard at the source and add fixtures covering the empty and non-object cases.

findings.title: statusOf asserts an `unknown` caught value into an object and dereferences it, so toAiError throws a TypeError instead of returning an AiError for null/undefined
findings.description: errors.ts:40 asserts an `unknown` caught value to `{ status?: unknown }` and immediately reads `.status`, so `toAiError(null)` and `toAiError(undefined)` throw a TypeError instead of returning an AiError — reproduced by execution (null/undefined throw; 'str', 42, true return undefined; {status:429} returns 429). That makes the declared contract `(error: unknown) => AiError` a lie for two of `unknown`'s inhabitants, on the single funnel that 16 call sites use to convert an untyped throw into a typed error, and the inconsistency is visible in the file itself: line 48 handles non-Error input with `String(error)` while line 40 does not. Reachability is the reason this is medium and not high: verified that every `throw` in src/ is `throw new <Error subclass>` or `throw toAiError(...)` with no bare `Promise.reject()`, so no in-repo producer triggers it — the exposure is entirely from third-party code reaching the `unknown` parameter, and neither the type system nor errors.test.ts (which only ever passes Error subclasses) would catch it if one appeared.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern and runtime behaviour CONFIRMED by execution; severity amended down because the finding's own honest reachability note is correct and I re-verified it. Pattern at errors.ts:39-42 verbatim: `function statusOf(error: unknown): number | undefined { const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status; ... }`. I reproduced the behaviour in node with the identical property read: null -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status')`; undefined -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')`; 'str' -> undefined; 42 -> undefined; true -> undefined; {status:429} -> 429. Exactly as claimed. The internal inconsistency is real: errors.ts:48 `error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)` explicitly anticipates non-Error input, and then line 40 dereferences the same value unguarded — and line 40 is only reached via the `else` at line 57, i.e. after the string branches have already run on a `String(null)` = 'null'. Blast radius CONFIRMED exactly as claimed by grep: 16 direct `toAiError(` call sites outside errors.ts — 9 in src/lib/ai (client.ts:26, chat.ts:18, chat.ts:37, quiz.ts:19, recommend.ts:41, summarize.ts:56, summarize.ts:77, summarize.ts:101, tts.ts:32) and 7 in UI (AppShell.tsx:48, ChatModal.tsx:72, BookDetail.tsx:169, BookDetail.tsx:189, EReader.tsx:213, QuizModal.tsx:65, ApiKeyDialog.tsx:33), plus 3 indirect via handleAiError (AppShell.tsx:47-56 -> LibraryPage.tsx:80, LibraryPage.tsx:98, AddBookModal via AppShell.tsx:196). REACHABILITY re-verified independently: `grep -rn 'throw |Promise.reject' src/` excluding `throw new ` returns only the 9 `throw toAiError(error)` lines — every other throw in src/ is `throw new <Error subclass>`, and there is no bare `Promise.reject()`. So no in-repo producer can trigger this today; the exposure is entirely third-party (the SDK, fetch, a future dependency). SDK check: node_modules/@google/genai/dist/web/index.mjs:14251 and :13971 both throw `new ApiError({...})`, which is an Error. Under the spec's scale, a latent defect with a trivial fix and no current in-repo trigger is medium ('erodes confidence and refactor safety'), not high.
findings.reachability: No in-repo path — verified that every `throw` in src/ is either `throw new <Error subclass>` or `throw toAiError(...)`, and there is no bare `Promise.reject()`. Triggered only if third-party code (the Gemini SDK, fetch, or a future dependency) rejects with null/undefined, at which point toAiError throws from inside a catch block, the rejection escapes the async handler (e.g. BookDetail.tsx:169), React error boundaries do not catch it, and the user sees no toast and a stuck spinner.
findings.blastRadius: 16 direct call sites (9 in src/lib/ai, 7 in src/components + src/app + src/features), plus 3 routed through handleAiError. Verified by grep, matches the claim exactly.

plain.title: Error handling itself throws when the thing being reported is empty
plain.what: The routine that inspects a caught failure assumes it is always an object and immediately reads a property from it. Nothing checks first.
plain.whyItMatters: Reporting a failure that is empty replaces the intended message with a second, unrelated error, hiding the original problem entirely.
plain.whatToDo: Confirm the value is a non-empty object before reading from it — a one-line guard with no behaviour change for anything currently reachable.

findings.title: QUIZ_SCHEMA leaves correctAnswerIndex as NUMBER and options unbounded, so the only enforcement layer permits ungradeable quizzes
findings.description: QUIZ_SCHEMA declares `correctAnswerIndex` as `Type.NUMBER` where the SDK offers `Type.INTEGER`, and leaves `options` without `minItems`/`maxItems`; the 0-3 range exists only as prose in a `description`, which is a prompt hint rather than a constraint. Tightening it (INTEGER + minimum/maximum + minItems/maxItems) is a cheap, compile-verified improvement to the request-side contract. Severity is medium rather than high because this is the schema-side mirror of an unvalidated-LLM-ingress defect already carried at higher severity by F005 (quiz.ts:16) and F040 (srs.ts newCard); the schema is a hint layer, not the enforcement gate, and Gemini structured output does not guarantee numeric range enforcement. Fix it alongside — never instead of — the runtime bounds check in `newCard`.

Both consumer failure modes verified by reading: an out-of-range index makes QuizModal.tsx:78 and :183 false for every option and `getPercentage()` (QuizModal.tsx:93) return 0, and the same index is persisted at QuizModal.tsx:52-61; an empty `options` makes QuizModal.tsx:182 render zero buttons so `isAnswered` never flips and the Next button at :242 stays `disabled` (the modal is still closable via the X at :167 or the backdrop at :99 — 'no way forward except closing it' is accurate). AMENDED DOWN because this is one of ten reports of a single defect: the unvalidated `correctAnswerIndex`/`options` pair from quiz.ts:16 is already carried by F005 (critical), F016, F017, F024, F025, F040, F052, F072 and F107. F032 is the request-side mirror — tightening the responseSchema is prompt/API-level defence-in-depth, not the enforcement gate; the gate is F005/F040. Its independent value is real but preventative, which is medium, not high.

plain.title: The quiz template permits ungradeable quizzes, and the range rule lives only in prose
plain.what: The template that constrains the AI's quiz output leaves the number of options unbounded and states the valid answer range only in an English description, which is a hint rather than a rule.
plain.whyItMatters: Since this template is the app's only shape enforcement, an ungradeable question can be produced and stored as valid.
plain.whatToDo: Use the template's own numeric and item-count constraints instead of describing them in prose.

findings.title: `category` is an unconstrained STRING in the schema, a plain `string` in TS, and the allowed list exists only in prompt prose
findings.description: Three layers disagree about what a category is. The Gemini schema declares `category: { type: Type.STRING }` with no `enum` and no `format: 'enum'`, even though `Schema.enum?: string[]` exists (genai.d.ts:12051). The allowed values live only as prose in prompts.ts:12 ('The category should be one of: Psychology, Productivity, Business, Technology, Philosophy, Health, Biography, Other'), which is a suggestion the model can ignore. `Book.category` (src/types.ts:33) is `string`. And src/types.ts:6-15 declares a `Category` enum with exactly those eight values that is imported and used nowhere in the codebase — dead code that documents an invariant nothing enforces. Failure: the model returns 'Self-Help' or 'Personal Development'; it is accepted, persisted, and LibraryPage.tsx:65 builds the category filter chips from `new Set(books.map(b => b.category))`, so the filter bar accretes near-duplicate one-book categories over time and StatsView's category breakdown fragments. Nothing crashes — this is silent data-quality drift the type system was in a position to prevent. Correct fix: add `enum` + `format: 'enum'` to the schema, change `Book['category']` to a literal union derived from the existing `Category` enum (or delete the enum), and coerce unknown values to 'Other' at the parse boundary — summarize.ts:26 already has the `|| 'Other'` fallback, it just never fires for a non-empty wrong string.
findings.verifierNote: All four layers verified. schemas.ts:8 `category: { type: Type.STRING }` has no enum, while genai.d.ts:12051 exposes `enum?: string[]` unused. The allowed values exist only as prose at prompts.ts:12. types.ts:33 declares `category: string`. And types.ts:6-15's `Category` enum is genuinely dead - a repo-wide grep for `Category` returns only that declaration, JSX label text (BookDetail.tsx:321, StatsView.tsx:133/138), a comment and unrelated identifiers (`activeCategory`, `categoryMap`); nothing imports it. summarize.ts:26 `category: data.category || 'Other'` confirms the finding's sharpest point: the fallback fires on empty/undefined only, never on a non-empty wrong string, so 'Self-Help' is accepted and persisted verbatim. LibraryPage.tsx:65 then builds the filter chips from `new Set(books.map((b) => b.category))`, so near-duplicate one-book categories accrete in the filter bar and StatsView.tsx:23-28's breakdown fragments. Medium is right: silent data-quality drift, no crash, and the codebase already contains the enum that documents the invariant nothing enforces.
findings.reachability: Every summary generation. One off-list category from the model permanently adds a chip to the library filter row and a bar to the stats breakdown for that profile.
findings.blastRadius: 1 schema field -> every generated Book; 2 display consumers (LibraryPage.tsx:65 filter chips, StatsView.tsx:23-28 breakdown) plus markdown.ts:13 export.
findings.suggestedPatch: schemas.ts:8 -> `category: { type: Type.STRING, format: 'enum', enum: Object.values(Category) }` (import the existing enum from types.ts, which finally gives it a use), and coerce at the parse boundary in summarize.ts:26 -> `category: (Object.values(Category) as string[]).includes(data.category ?? '') ? data.category! : 'Other'`. Optionally narrow `Book['category']` to `` `${Category}` ``. Risk: narrowing the Book field breaks existing records with off-list categories, so either keep the field as `string` and rely on the coercion, or ship a one-time migration.

plain.title: A book's category is unconstrained everywhere except in the prompt's wording
plain.what: Three layers describe categories differently: the AI template allows any text, the app type allows any text, and the permitted list exists only as prose in the prompt.
plain.whyItMatters: The AI can return a category outside the intended set, which then becomes a filter chip in the library that matches exactly one book.
plain.whatToDo: Put the permitted list into the AI template as an enumeration and reuse the same list in the app.

findings.title: `rating` and `readingTimeMinutes` carry their ranges only in description text and are persisted unvalidated
findings.description: Both are `Type.NUMBER` with the intended range stated only in a `description` — 'A rating from 1 to 5' and 'Estimated time in minutes... assume 250 words per minute'. `Schema.minimum`/`Schema.maximum` (genai.d.ts:12064,12072) are available and unused, and `Book.rating` / `Book.readingTimeMinutes` (src/types.ts:36,47) are unbranded `number`s, so neither layer rejects 8.7, -3 or 100000. summarize.ts:28-29 applies only `?? 0` / `?? 5`, which fire on nullish values, not out-of-range ones. AddBookModal.tsx:74 happens to overwrite `rating` with the user's slider value, but LibraryPage.tsx:90-94 (the 'add from recommendation' path) persists the model's number verbatim. Failure: BookCard.tsx:100 renders `{book.rating}/5` producing '8.7/5'; BookDetail.tsx:278-287 renders a five-star row via `num <= Math.round(book.rating)` so a rating of 8.7 lights every star and prints '8.7' beside them; StatsView.tsx:20 averages ratings across finished books and reports a skewed average forever. No crash, but permanently wrong displayed data with no correction path for the rating that came from the recommendation flow. Correct fix: `minimum`/`maximum` in the schema plus a clamp at the parse boundary — the natural home is `toGenerated` in summarize.ts, which already normalises every other field.

13 |     readingTimeMinutes: {
  14 |       type: Type.NUMBER,
  15 |       description:
  16 |         'Estimated time in minutes to read the generated summary, insights, and steps (NOT the original book). Assume 250 words per minute.',
  17 |     },
  18 |     rating: {
  19 |       type: Type.NUMBER,
  20 |       description: "A rating from 1 to 5 based on the book's critical acclaim and value.",
  21 |     },
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed against source. schemas.ts:13-21 declares readingTimeMinutes and rating as bare `Type.NUMBER` with the range only in a `description`, while genai.d.ts:12073 `minimum?` and :12065 `maximum?` sit unused. types.ts:36/47 are unbranded `number`. summarize.ts:28-29 applies `rating: data.rating ?? 0` and `readingTimeMinutes: data.readingTimeMinutes ?? 5` - nullish coalescing only, so 8.7, -3 and 100000 all pass through. The two paths are as claimed: AddBookModal.tsx:74 overwrites `rating` with the user's slider value, but LibraryPage.tsx:91-94 (add-from-recommendation) spreads `...book` straight into addBook, persisting the model's number verbatim with no user override. Display consequences verified: BookCard.tsx:100 renders `{book.rating}/5` -> '8.7/5'; BookDetail.tsx:278/282 light every star via `num <= Math.round(book.rating)` and :287 prints the raw value; StatsView.tsx:20 folds it into the average forever. Medium is right - no crash, permanently wrong displayed data with no correction path on the recommendation route. Note this compounds F061: the same average is polluted from both ends (Goodreads sentinel 0s and unclamped model ratings).
findings.reachability: Library -> Recommendations carousel -> preview a recommendation -> summarizeBook returns rating 8.7 -> LibraryPage.tsx:91 persists it -> the card shows '8.7/5', BookDetail lights all five stars, and the stats average is skewed permanently.
findings.blastRadius: 2 schema fields -> every generated Book; 1 unguarded write path (LibraryPage.tsx:91-94); 4 display sites (BookCard.tsx:100, BookDetail.tsx:278/282/287, StatsView.tsx:20, markdown export).
findings.suggestedPatch: schemas.ts:18-21 -> add `minimum: 1, maximum: 5`; :13-17 -> add `minimum: 1, maximum: 600`. Then clamp in summarize.ts's toGenerated, which already normalises every other field: `const clamp = (n: number | undefined, lo: number, hi: number, dflt: number) => (typeof n === 'number' && Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, Math.round(n))) : dflt);` used as `rating: clamp(data.rating, 1, 5, 0)` and `readingTimeMinutes: clamp(data.readingTimeMinutes, 1, 600, 5)`. Risk: rounding changes existing snapshot expectations in summarize tests; existing out-of-range records are not repaired by this and would need a migration if any exist.

plain.title: Rating and reading-time ranges are stated only in prose, then stored unchecked
plain.what: The AI template describes the valid ranges for rating and reading time in an English description rather than as numeric limits, even though the template supports real limits.
plain.whyItMatters: Out-of-range values are stored as-is and then feed the statistics screen, producing an impossible average rating or a wildly wrong total reading time.
plain.whatToDo: Use the template's numeric limits and clamp the values when converting the reply.

findings.title: `?? []` / `|| 'fallback'` in toGenerated guard only nullish values, so a wrong-typed field is persisted and crashes every later read
findings.description: `toGenerated` (src/lib/ai/summarize.ts:34-37) defends only against nullish values: `data.keyInsights ?? []` passes a non-array straight through into `Summary.keyInsights`, declared `string[]` at src/types.ts:59, which is then persisted to IndexedDB (useLibrary.tsx:48) and read by seven call sites that assume the array (prompts.ts:36,49,67,70,82; markdown.ts:25,28), each of which would throw `TypeError`. The lying type and the missing guard are both real. Severity lowered to medium because verification could not establish a producer mismatch: the only ingress is Gemini with `responseSchema` attached (summarize.ts:49,70) declaring those fields ARRAY-of-STRING, so a string here is a model contract violation rather than an expected shape — and the reachable half of the original claim (a structurally valid but empty summary being persisted) is already carried at high by F034. Sibling F096 (the identical `?? []` over localStorage in migrate.ts:127) is likewise medium.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern present exactly as quoted: src/lib/ai/summarize.ts:34-37 uses `||` for the two strings and `?? []` for the two arrays, so only nullish values are defended; the `as RawBookResponse` at :52 and :73 means the compiler never sees the gap. The lying type is real — the result is assigned to `Summary.keyInsights`/`actionableSteps`, declared `string[]` at src/types.ts:59-60, and persisted with no re-validation via useLibrary.tsx:48 (`summaryRepo.upsert`), reached from AddBookModal.tsx:69-79 and LibraryPage.tsx:90-94. Consumers verified: prompts.ts:36 (`summary.keyInsights.join('\n')`), :49, :67, :70, :82, and markdown.ts:25 / :28 (`.map`) — all throw `TypeError` on a string. AMENDED DOWN to medium on spec verification-criterion 2: I could not establish a producer/runtime mismatch. The only ingress here is Gemini with `responseSchema: GENERIC_BOOK_SCHEMA` attached at :49 and :70, which declares those fields `Type.ARRAY` of `Type.STRING` (schemas.ts:11-12), so constrained decoding makes a string-where-array response a contract violation by the model rather than an expected shape. The genuinely reachable half of the finding — an empty array reaching storage — is F034's `|| '{}'` path, already reported at high. For consistency, note the identical `?? []` defect over a strictly more attacker-reachable source (localStorage, migrate.ts:127) is rated medium as F096.

Possible (structured output is best-effort, and per F031 a schema typo would silently disable it entirely) but not demonstrated. The empty-array outcome is reachable on the ordinary add-a-book path, but that is F034's mechanism.

plain.title: Summary fields are defaulted in a way that lets wrong-typed AI values through
plain.what: When converting the AI's reply, missing lists are replaced with empty ones. That mechanism only substitutes for absent values; a value of the wrong kind is passed along untouched.
plain.whyItMatters: A non-list value gets stored where a list is expected and then crashes every later read of that summary, including the export and the markdown view.
plain.whatToDo: Check the shape rather than just the presence of each field before it is stored.

findings.title: toGenerated promises a fully-formed Book and Summary but its `??` and `||` defaults only guard null/undefined, so a wrong-typed model field is persisted as a real summary
findings.description: `toGenerated(...): GeneratedBook` declares `keyInsights: string[]`, `actionableSteps: string[]`, `rating: number` and `readingTimeMinutes: number` as guaranteed. Its inputs come from `JSON.parse(response.text || '{}') as RawBookResponse` (lines 52 and 73). `RawBookResponse` is honest about ABSENCE — every field is optional, with a comment explaining why — but says nothing about WRONG TYPE, and `??`/`||` only substitute for null/undefined. A model that returns `keyInsights` as a single string rather than an array, or `rating` as `"4"`, passes straight through: `data.keyInsights ?? []` keeps the string. The result is written to IndexedDB as a real `Summary` by useLibrary.addBook -> summaryRepo.upsert. Broken consumers: BookDetail.tsx:470 runs `(summary?.keyInsights ?? []).map(...)` — `.map` is not a function on a string, so the book detail route throws to the error boundary every time that book is opened; markdown.ts:24-25 does `keyInsights.length > 0` (a string passes) then `.map` and throws the same way, killing Markdown export. This is the same file as the already-known sentinel at line 99 but a distinct defect at lines 22-41, and unlike that one it corrupts stored data rather than just labelling it.

plain.title: Wrong-typed AI fields are converted into a finished book and stored as real
plain.what: The conversion from an AI reply into a stored book promises complete lists and real numbers. Its defaults only fill in fields that are entirely absent; a field of the wrong kind passes through untouched.
plain.whyItMatters: The raw reply shape is honest about fields being missing, and the conversion discards that honesty. A wrong-typed value is then stored permanently and breaks every screen that reads it.
plain.whatToDo: Coerce each field by checking its shape rather than only its presence, so the promised type is true by construction.

findings.title: The audio part's mimeType is discarded and the PCM format is hardcoded, so a format change produces silently corrupt WAV
findings.description: Line 27 reaches into `response.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.inlineData?.data` and takes only `data`. The sibling `inlineData.mimeType` — which Gemini TTS populates with the actual format descriptor, e.g. `audio/L16;codec=pcm;rate=24000` — is never read. `pcmToWavBlob` (src/lib/audio/wav.ts:1-3,12) hardcodes SAMPLE_RATE 24000, NUM_CHANNELS 1, BITS_PER_SAMPLE 16 and stamps those into the RIFF header at wav.ts:22-27. Nothing at any layer checks that the bytes actually match: `base64ToBytes` returns `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` for any decodable input and the header is written unconditionally. If a model revision returns a different sample rate or channel count, the WAV header lies about the payload and the audio plays at the wrong pitch and speed — a silent wrong-output failure, not an exception, and the blob is then persisted to the `blobs` store and replayed from cache. The declared parameter type `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` describes the container but carries no information about the encoding it must be, which is exactly the case for a branded/validated boundary. Correct fix: read `mimeType` alongside `data`, parse the `rate=` and `codec=` parameters, and either pass them into `pcmToWavBlob` or throw an `AiError` of kind `'malformed'` when they differ from what the WAV writer assumes. Verified positive worth recording: line 28's `if (!base64Audio) throw` correctly narrows the SDK's optional chain instead of using `!` — this file contains no non-null assertion. Blast radius: 2 call sites (BookDetail.tsx:159, EReader.tsx:203).
findings.verifierNote: Pattern present and exact. src/lib/ai/tts.ts:27 reads `response.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.inlineData?.data` and line 30 pipes it into `pcmToWavBlob(base64ToBytes(...))`; `mimeType` is never read anywhere in the file. I confirmed the sibling field exists on the SDK type: node_modules/@google/genai/dist/genai.d.ts declares `Blob_2 { data?: string; displayName?: string; mimeType?: string }` with the doc comment 'Required. The IANA standard MIME type of the source data.' So the authoritative format IS returned and IS discarded. src/lib/audio/wav.ts:1-3 hardcodes 24000/1/16 and stamps them at :23-27 unconditionally. The finding's verified-positive is also correct: line 28's `if (!base64Audio) throw` narrows the optional chain rather than using `!`, and there is no `!` in this file. Kept at medium rather than amended up because verification criterion 2 cuts the other way - the runtime data currently DOES match the claimed format (Gemini TTS documents 24kHz mono 16-bit PCM), so this is latent boundary erasure, not a live mismatch. Report note: F081 and F082 are the same single defect filed twice from different lots (L05 producer side, L07 consumer side) and were not deduplicated in aggregate.json.
findings.reachability: Reachable on every audio generation: src/components/BookDetail.tsx:159 and src/components/EReader.tsx:203 both call `generateAudioSummary`. The resulting WAV is persisted to the `blobs` store and replayed from cache, so a mislabelled header would survive reload. The trigger requires a Gemini model or voice-pipeline format change; no current response exhibits it.
findings.blastRadius: 2 non-test call sites of `generateAudioSummary` (BookDetail.tsx:159, EReader.tsx:203); 1 non-test call site of `pcmToWavBlob` (tts.ts:30). Recounted by grep excluding *.test.ts.

plain.title: The audio format the service reports is discarded and a fixed one is assumed instead
plain.what: When speech audio comes back, the app takes the bytes and ignores the format label sitting next to them, then stamps on a hard-coded format header.
plain.whyItMatters: If the service ever returns a different sample rate or bit depth, the app produces audio that plays at the wrong speed or as noise, with no error anywhere.
plain.whatToDo: Read the reported format and refuse to build a file when it is not the expected one.

findings.title: base64 suite has two happy-path tests only; base64ToBytes is total in its type but throws on the one input path it serves
findings.description: src/lib/base64.test.ts has exactly two happy-path tests (lines 5-12), neither of which feeds invalid base64, an empty string, a data-URL prefix or a non-string, so the decoder is proven only against input the tests themselves encoded — and migrate.test.ts:42 (`btoa('fake pdf bytes')`) has the same self-encoding property. The gap is real, but it is the test-side mirror of F037 (the total `(string) => Uint8Array` signature that is actually partial) and duplicates F006's integration-level version of the same claim, so it is medium rather than high. Track it as the test half of F037's fix: the valuable test is the one that pins the corrected contract, not one that asserts today's DOMException.
findings.verifierNote: Every claim is factually correct. src/lib/base64.test.ts contains exactly two tests (lines 5-8 round-trip six clean bytes, lines 10-12 decode a hand-written 'Qm9va1N1bQ=='); there is no invalid-input, empty-string, data-URL-prefix or non-string case anywhere in the 13-line file. The 'proven only against input the tests themselves encoded' point holds for the migration suite too — src/lib/storage/migrate.test.ts:42 seeds `pdfData: btoa('fake pdf bytes')`, so it likewise cannot reach the throw. Rating a third mirror `high` triple-counts one defect. There is also a design point: a test that pins today's DOMException is near-worthless — the test worth writing is the one that pins the FIXED contract from F037, so this finding should be folded into F037's fix rather than tracked as its own high-severity item.

plain.title: The encoding tests only cover inputs the tests themselves produced
plain.what: The two tests for the encoding helpers use only well-formed data they generated. Invalid input, empty input and prefixed input are never tried.

findings.title: Google Books HTTP response asserted into a shape with zero runtime validation
findings.description:
`await response.json()` is `any` in lib.dom; the `as {...}` at L12-14 is a pure assertion over a third-party API's live output with no guard, no schema, and no narrowing. The declared shape is fiction: nothing at runtime proves `items` is an array or that `imageLinks` values are strings. CORRECT BEHAVIOR: parse into `unknown` and narrow with a type guard (or validate the picked URL with `typeof url === 'string'`) before use.

CONCRETE FAILURE: the cast declares `imageLinks?: Record<string, string>`, so L24 calls `url.replace(/^http:\/\//, 'https://')` on a value the compiler believes is a `string`. `if (url)` filters null/undefined/'' but NOT a truthy non-string. If the endpoint ever returns a non-string in `imageLinks` (or a differently-shaped 200 body — an error envelope, a captive-portal/proxy interstitial that happens to be valid JSON), `url.replace` is a `TypeError: url.replace is not a function`.

MITIGATION THAT CAPS SEVERITY AT MEDIUM (verified, not assumed): `res.ok` IS checked first at L10 (so 404/500 bodies are never parsed as a success shape — a real positive here), every field is optional-chained, and the sole caller `fetchCover` (src/lib/covers/index.ts:13-20) wraps the call in try/catch and falls through to `placeholderCover`. So today the crash degrades to a placeholder cover, not a user-visible error.

BLAST RADIUS: `fetchCover` <- src/lib/ai/summarize.ts:53 and src/lib/ai/recommend.ts:37 (2 call sites, both AI paths). NOT on the Goodreads import path. This would be HIGH, not medium, the moment anyone calls the exported `fetchGoogleBooksCover` directly without the caller's try/catch (see L06-F04).
findings.verifierNote: Pattern present verbatim at src/lib/covers/googleBooks.ts:12-14: `const data = (await response.json()) as { items?: { volumeInfo?: { imageLinks?: Record<string, string> } }[] };`. `response.json()` is `Promise<any>` in lib.dom, so this is a pure assertion over live third-party JSON with no guard, schema, or narrowing. The concrete failure is real: because `imageLinks` is asserted `Record<string, string>`, line 24 calls `url.replace(/^http:\/\//, 'https://')` on a value the compiler believes is a string, and `if (url)` filters falsy but not truthy-non-string, so a numeric or object value is `TypeError: url.replace is not a function`. All three claimed mitigations are present in current source: `if (!response.ok) continue` at :10, every field optional-chained at :16-23, and the sole caller's try/catch at src/lib/covers/index.ts:14-19 falling through to `placeholderCover` at :21. Medium is right: the boundary is genuinely unvalidated (the spec's highest-priority category) but every failure degrades to a placeholder cover rather than a user-visible error.
findings.reachability: Reachable whenever a summary or recommendation is generated: src/lib/ai/summarize.ts:53 and src/lib/ai/recommend.ts:37 both await `fetchCover`, which calls this provider first. NOT on the Goodreads import path (useLibrary.tsx:158 uses `coverForIsbn`), so a large import stays free as CLAUDE.md requires.
findings.blastRadius: 1 direct caller (src/lib/covers/index.ts:13, via the lookup array); 2 transitive non-test call sites through `fetchCover` (summarize.ts:53, recommend.ts:37). Recounted excluding src/lib/covers/index.test.ts.

plain.title: The Google Books cover response is assumed to have the expected shape
plain.what: The reply from the cover-lookup service is treated as the shape the app wants without any checking, because the browser's own network types provide no guarantees.
plain.whyItMatters: A changed or partial third-party response produces broken cover images or failures inside the fallback chain instead of a clean 'no cover found'.
plain.whatToDo: Read the response as unknown and narrow it step by step to the two fields actually used.

findings.title: OpenLibrary search response asserted to `{ docs?: { cover_i?: number }[] }` without validation
findings.description:
Same class as L06-F01: `await response.json()` is `any`, and the `as { docs?: { cover_i?: number }[] }` at L6 asserts a shape over a live third-party API with no runtime check. OpenLibrary's `search.json` returns notoriously sparse and inconsistent records; nothing here proves `docs` is an array or that `cover_i` is a number. CORRECT BEHAVIOR: narrow via `typeof coverId === 'number' && Number.isInteger(coverId)` before building the URL.

CONCRETE FAILURE: if `cover_i` arrives as a string or any other JSON scalar, the cast says `number`, the template at L8 interpolates it regardless, and `Book.coverImageUrl` is persisted to IndexedDB pointing at a URL that 404s. The compiler cannot see it because the assertion told it not to look. There is no crash here (unlike F01) because only string interpolation touches the value — which is why this is medium, not high.

MITIGATION (verified): `res.ok` IS checked at L4 before parsing, `docs?.[0]?.cover_i` is fully optional-chained, and `fetchCover` (src/lib/covers/index.ts:13-20) catches any throw. A bad URL degrades to the `onError` placeholder swap in src/components/BookCard.tsx:18/27.

BLAST RADIUS: reached only via `fetchCover` (2 call sites: src/lib/ai/summarize.ts:53, src/lib/ai/recommend.ts:37).
findings.verifierNote: Pattern present verbatim at src/lib/covers/openLibrary.ts:6: `const data = (await response.json()) as { docs?: { cover_i?: number }[] };`, then :7 `data.docs?.[0]?.cover_i` and :8 interpolates it into the URL. Same class as F085 and correctly rated one notch less dangerous: only string interpolation touches the value, so a non-number `cover_i` yields a dead URL rather than a TypeError. Mitigations verified in current source: `if (!response.ok) return null` at :4, full optional chaining at :7, `fetchCover`'s try/catch at index.ts:14-19. I additionally verified the downstream degradation: src/components/BookCard.tsx defines `handleError` (~line 27) which swaps in `placeholderCover(book.title)` on image load failure, plus a `useEffect` (~lines 15-24) that pre-empts empty/'null' URLs - so a bad cover URL is invisible to the user. Held at medium rather than amended down because the pattern is the spec's highest-priority category (unvalidated assertion over a live third-party API) and the bad value is PERSISTED to `Book.coverImageUrl` in IndexedDB, where nothing re-validates it on read.
findings.reachability: Reached via `fetchCover` whenever Google Books returns nothing: src/lib/ai/summarize.ts:53 and src/lib/ai/recommend.ts:37. OpenLibrary's search.json is documented-sparse, so a missing or oddly-typed `cover_i` is an ordinary response, not exotic.
findings.blastRadius: 1 direct caller (src/lib/covers/index.ts:13); 2 transitive non-test call sites. Same reach as F085.

plain.title: The OpenLibrary cover response is assumed to have the expected shape
plain.what: The reply from the second cover service is likewise treated as the expected shape with no checking.
plain.whyItMatters: The service does return other shapes for some queries, and the code would read a field that is not there rather than fall back cleanly.
plain.whatToDo: Narrow the response instead of assuming it, and fall back to the placeholder when the shape does not match.

findings.title: Every CSV indexed access is typed as a definite value; the runtime guards are invisible to the compiler
findings.description:
`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is OFF (tsconfig.json has `strict: true` but not this flag), so in the CSV parser every `array[i]` is typed as a definite value when the runtime value is `undefined` for a short or ragged row. IMPORTANT AND HONEST FRAMING: this file is already correctly guarded at runtime — this is a refactor-safety finding, not a live crash. The unusual value here is that enabling the flag would compile CLEAN on this file, because the guards already exist; it would simply convert them from optional discipline into a compiler-enforced requirement.

ENUMERATED SITES (5, this lot):
- goodreads.ts:29 `const char = text[i]` — typed `string`, would be `string | undefined`; provably in-bounds via the loop condition, so no live bug.
- goodreads.ts:33 `text[i + 1] === '"'` — genuinely `undefined` at the final character; the `===` comparison is safe either way.
- goodreads.ts:82 `(table[0] ?? [])` — guarded by `??`, which the compiler currently believes is unreachable.
- goodreads.ts:96 `(cells[index] ?? '').trim()` — THE ONE THAT MATTERS (see below).
- covers/openLibrary.ts:7 `data.docs?.[0]?.cover_i` — the second `?.` is the only thing handling an empty `docs` array, and the compiler thinks it is redundant.

NAMED CRASH: at L96, for a ragged row — a Goodreads export whose final line is truncated, or any row with fewer commas than the header — `cells[index]` IS `undefined` at runtime while the compiler insists it is `string`. Only the `?? ''` prevents `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')`. That throw would escape `parseGoodreadsCsv`, be caught by src/features/library/GoodreadsImport.tsx:30, and surface as the generic 'Could not read that file.' toast — the user's entire library import fails with no diagnostic. The guard is one character of defensive coding standing between a correct import and total failure, and the type system currently offers zero protection if it is ever deleted as apparently-dead code.

TOOLING NOTE (checked, not assumed): eslint.config.js uses `tseslint.configs.recommended`, NOT `recommendedTypeChecked`/`strictTypeChecked`, so `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` is NOT enabled — no linter will currently flag these `??` guards as dead. The risk is therefore a human or AI reader trusting the declared `string` type, not an automated cleanup.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed, and I MEASURED the finding's central claim rather than reasoning about it. tsconfig.json has `strict: true` without `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. Running `npx tsc --noEmit --noUncheckedIndexedAccess -p tsconfig.json` produces exactly 10 errors project-wide, distributed as QuizModal.tsx 5 (78, 178, 182, 183, 232), BookDetail.tsx 3 (71, 79, 85), EReader.tsx 1 (395), AddBookModal.tsx 1 (43) - and ZERO in src/lib/goodreads.ts and ZERO in src/lib/covers/openLibrary.ts. The finding's claim that this file would compile clean under the flag is therefore true and now measured; the whole of src/lib/** is already clean. All five enumerated sites are present in current source: goodreads.ts:29 `const char = text[i]`, :33 `text[i + 1] === '"'`, :82 `(table[0] ?? [])`, :96 `(cells[index] ?? '').trim()`, and covers/openLibrary.ts:7 `data.docs?.[0]?.cover_i`. The named crash at :96 is real for a ragged row: `parseCsv` (:22-66) pushes rows of whatever length the line had, so `cells[index]` for a high index is genuinely `undefined` at runtime while the compiler insists it is `string`; only the `?? ''` prevents `TypeError: ...trim()`. The tooling note checks out too - eslint.config.js uses `tseslint.configs.recommended`, so `no-unnecessary-condition` is off and nothing will flag these guards as dead. Medium is exactly the spec's 'erodes refactor safety but isn't on a critical path'.
findings.reachability: No live crash - the runtime guards are all present and correct. The risk is a future editor (human or AI) deleting a `?? ''` that the declared `string` type makes look redundant; that would surface as src/features/library/GoodreadsImport.tsx:30 catching the throw and showing the generic 'Could not read that file.' toast for the user's entire import.
findings.blastRadius: 5 sites in this lot; 10 sites project-wide would need a fix to enable the flag, all in 4 component files (measured, not estimated). src/lib/** needs no change at all.
findings.suggestedPatch: Add `"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true` to tsconfig.json's compilerOptions and close the 10 measured errors - each is an `array[i]` read fixable with an `if (!x) return` guard or a `?? fallback` at QuizModal.tsx 78/178/182/183/232, BookDetail.tsx 71/79/85, EReader.tsx 395, AddBookModal.tsx 43. Risk: a real (if small) diff across 4 UI files, so land it as its own commit; note that several of those same lines are already flagged by higher-severity findings, so sequence this after them.

plain.title: The CSV parser's own safety checks are invisible to the compiler
plain.what: Because one compiler option is switched off, every row and column read in the parser is described as definitely present even where the author added runtime checks for the opposite.
plain.whyItMatters: The checks are correct today, but nothing keeps them correct: deleting one would compile cleanly and only fail on a ragged spreadsheet.
plain.whatToDo: Enable the option and close the ten measured sites; none of them are in the core library code.

findings.title: CSV `My Rating` coerced with parseInt and stored unvalidated as an unbounded `number`
findings.description:
`GoodreadsRow.rating` is declared `number` (L7) and produced by `Number.parseInt` over raw file content. The `Number.isFinite` guard at L111 is CORRECT and does kill `NaN` (verified negative — the brief's NaN-propagation hypothesis does not materialise; `Number.isFinite`, not the coercing global `isFinite`, is used). What is missing is any DOMAIN validation: `parseInt` is a lenient parser typed as a total function, so `'-3'` -> -3, `'4.7'` -> 4 (silent truncation), `'12'` -> 12, `'3 stars'` -> 3. All are finite, so all are stored. CORRECT BEHAVIOR: clamp/validate to Goodreads' 0-5 domain at the parse boundary (a `Rating` branded type or a `>= 0 && <= 5` guard), rather than trusting `number`.

CONCRETE FAILURE: the value flows unvalidated to src/features/library/useLibrary.tsx:156 -> `bookRepo.create` (src/lib/storage/repo.ts:51, which performs no validation — its param type is just `Omit<Book,'id'|'addedAt'>`) -> IndexedDB. It is then consumed by src/components/StatsView.tsx:20 `(finished.reduce((acc, b) => acc + b.rating, 0) / finished.length).toFixed(1)`, so one out-of-range row silently reports an average like `8.4` on a 5-point scale; and by src/lib/markdown.ts:14 `**Rating:** ${book.rating}/5`, which exports `-3/5` into the user's markdown. src/components/BookDetail.tsx:278 `num <= Math.round(book.rating)` renders all five stars lit for any rating >= 5 and zero for a negative — wrong, but no crash. Because the record is persisted, the corruption survives reload; nothing re-validates on read.

TRIGGER (honest): Goodreads itself only writes 0-5, so the realistic entry point is a hand-edited export or a non-Goodreads CSV that happens to carry a `My Rating` header — a plausible user path, not the default one. Hence medium, not high.

BLAST RADIUS: 4 consumers of `Book.rating` (StatsView, BookDetail, BookCard.tsx:100, markdown.ts).
findings.verifierNote: Pattern present exactly: src/lib/goodreads.ts:104 `const rating = Number.parseInt(cell(ratingAt), 10)` and :111 `rating: Number.isFinite(rating) ? rating : 0`, against `GoodreadsRow.rating: number` at :7. The finding's verified-negative is correct - `Number.isFinite` (not the coercing global `isFinite`) is used, so NaN really is killed and the NaN-propagation hypothesis does not materialise. What survives is the domain gap: parseInt is lenient and typed total, so '-3' -> -3, '4.7' -> 4, '12' -> 12, '3 stars' -> 3 all pass the finite check and are stored. I traced the flow and every consumer it names exists in current source: src/features/library/useLibrary.tsx:156 `rating: row.rating` -> `bookRepo.create` (src/lib/storage/repo.ts:51-61, which validates nothing; its input type is just `Omit<Book,'id'|'addedAt'> & Partial<...>`) -> IndexedDB. Read sites: src/components/StatsView.tsx:20 averages into `.toFixed(1)`, src/lib/markdown.ts:14 exports `${book.rating}/5`, src/components/BookDetail.tsx:215/278/282/287, src/components/BookCard.tsx:100. Medium is right and the finding is honest about why: Goodreads itself only emits 0-5, so the trigger is a hand-edited export or a foreign CSV carrying a 'My Rating' column.
findings.reachability: User path: import a CSV that is not a pristine Goodreads export (hand-edited, or exported from another tool with a 'My Rating' header). The out-of-range rating is persisted and survives reload - nothing re-validates on read - showing e.g. an 8.4 average on a 5-point scale in StatsView or '-3/5' in the markdown export. No crash.
findings.blastRadius: 1 producer (goodreads.ts:104) -> 1 write path (useLibrary.tsx:156) -> 5 non-test read sites of `Book.rating` across 4 files (StatsView.tsx:20, markdown.ts:14, BookCard.tsx:100, BookDetail.tsx:215/278/282/287). Recounted excluding tests.
findings.suggestedPatch:
Clamp at the parse boundary in src/lib/goodreads.ts:111:
  rating: Number.isFinite(rating) ? Math.min(5, Math.max(0, Math.trunc(rating))) : 0,
Risk: none for valid exports (0-5 unchanged); an out-of-range hand-edited value is clamped rather than silently stored, which is the strictly safer failure. A `Rating` branded type is the fuller fix but would touch all 5 read sites and is not worth it here.

plain.title: A spreadsheet rating is converted to a number and stored with no upper or lower bound
plain.what: The rating column is converted from text to a number and stored without confirming it falls within the one-to-five range the rest of the app assumes.
plain.whyItMatters: A hand-edited or foreign spreadsheet can put an arbitrary number into the average-rating statistic and into the star display.
plain.whatToDo: Clamp the value to the valid range where it is parsed.

findings.title: parseGoodreadsCsv returns 'Unknown' and 0 as not-found sentinels typed as real author and rating values, and StatsView averages the 0s into the user's rating, silently deflating it
findings.description: `GoodreadsRow.author: string` and `rating: number` (lines 5-7) claim every row carries a real author and a real rating. The parser manufactures sentinels for the missing case: line 109 substitutes the literal string `'Unknown'` for a blank author cell, and line 111 substitutes `0` for a missing or unparseable 'My Rating' — which is exactly what Goodreads writes for a book you read but never rated. Nothing downstream distinguishes sentinel from datum, because the types cannot express the difference. Exact input: a real Goodreads export in which some read books are unrated (the common case). Broken consumer: useLibrary.tsx:156 persists `rating: row.rating` as a genuine Book rating with `status: 'Finished'`, and StatsView.tsx:18-20 computes `finished.reduce((acc, b) => acc + b.rating, 0) / finished.length` over ALL finished books — so every unrated import drags the displayed average rating toward zero, with no indication why. BookCard.tsx:100 also renders a confident '0/5' badge for those books. The same sentinel is minted a second time at migrate.ts:113 (`rating: legacy.rating ?? 0`), so it travels in a pack.
findings.evidence:
107:     rows.push({
108:       title,
109:       author: cell(authorAt) || 'Unknown',                 // sentinel typed as a real author
111:       rating: Number.isFinite(rating) ? rating : 0,        // sentinel typed as a real rating

src/components/StatsView.tsx
 18:     const avgRating =
 19:       finished.length > 0
 20:         ? (finished.reduce((acc, b) => acc + b.rating, 0) / finished.length).toFixed(1)
findings.suggestedPatch: Make absence representable: change `GoodreadsRow.rating` to `rating?: number` and emit `undefined` (not 0) at goodreads.ts:111 when the cell is blank or unparseable, then map it to `rating: row.rating ?? 0` at the persistence boundary only. The real fix for the visible bug is at StatsView.tsx:18 — average over `finished.filter((b) => b.rating > 0)` and fall back to '—' when none qualify. Risk: `Book.rating` stays a required number, so this is a display-layer change plus one optional field; goodreads.test.ts assertions on the 0 default will need updating.

plain.title: Imported books with no author or rating are given fake values that the statistics treat as real
plain.what: The spreadsheet parser substitutes the literal word 'Unknown' for a blank author and zero for a missing rating, and both are stored as though they were genuine data.
plain.whyItMatters: The statistics screen averages those zeros into your rating, so importing an unrated library silently deflates the figure shown. 'Unknown' becomes a real author name in filters and exports.
plain.whatToDo: Make absence representable — leave the rating unset rather than zero — and exclude unset ratings from the average.

findings.title: Migration fixtures are always well-formed, so a throwing migration that permanently hangs boot is green
findings.description: src/lib/storage/migrate.test.ts's only fixture, seedLegacyLocalStorage (lines 8-62), always writes syntactically perfect, correctly-shaped data: a real array of book objects and valid raw base64 for pdfData. All 8 tests run that one happy path, so the suite proves only that the migration works on data the test itself wrote in the correct shape. The untested failure path is real and its consequence is severe: migrate.ts:58's `JSON.parse(raw) as T` catches only syntax errors, migrate.ts:99's `?? []` rescues only `null`, and migrate.ts:101's `for...of` throws on any non-iterable; ProfileContext.tsx:30-42 awaits migrateLegacyData() inside a `void`-ed async IIFE, so a throw skips `setIsLoading(false)` (line 41), leaves the app on App.tsx's loading spinner forever, bypasses the error boundary as an unhandled rejection, and — because MIGRATION_MARKER is written last at migrate.ts:149 — repeats identically on every reload. Note that two failure shapes the original write-up cited are not actually producible by this app's predecessor: commit 670b5fe stripped the data-URL prefix before storing pdfData (670b5fe:components/AddBookModal.tsx:28) and always wrote a JSON array to the library key (670b5fe:App.tsx:212). Triggering the crash therefore requires DevTools, an extension, or a same-origin key collision — which is why this is a Medium coverage gap rather than a Critical production defect.

findings.verifierNote: The coverage gap is real; two of the specific failure shapes cited are factually wrong, and they were carrying the Critical rating. CONFIRMED: seedLegacyLocalStorage (migrate.test.ts:8-62) is the only fixture, and all 8 tests use it or an empty array (line 147). It always writes a real JSON array of well-shaped book objects (lines 27-60) and valid base64 via `btoa('fake pdf bytes')` (line 42). The production fragility is also exactly as analysed: migrate.ts:58 `JSON.parse(raw) as T` catches only syntax errors; migrate.ts:99's `?? []` rescues only `null`; migrate.ts:101 `for (const legacy of legacyBooks)` throws on a non-iterable; ProfileContext.tsx:30-42 awaits migrateLegacyData() as the first statement of a `void`-ed async IIFE so a throw skips `setIsLoading(false)` at line 41 and surfaces only as an unhandled rejection (App.tsx:12-18 then shows the spinner forever); and MIGRATION_MARKER really is written last, at migrate.ts:149. REFUTED SUB-CLAIMS: (1) 'a data-URL-prefixed data:application/pdf;base64,... value — the obvious shape for the original app to have stored' is wrong. The original app at commit 670b5fe explicitly strips the prefix: 670b5fe:components/AddBookModal.tsx:28 is `const base64 = (reader.result as string).split(',')[1];`. It stored RAW base64, which is precisely what the fixture's `btoa(...)` models. (2) 'valid JSON of the WRONG type' under a `booksum_library_*` key cannot be produced by any shipped BookSum: 670b5fe:App.tsx:212 is `localStorage.setItem(userLibraryKey, JSON.stringify(books))` with `books: BookInsight[]` — always an array. Reaching either failure therefore requires DevTools, an extension, or a foreign app colliding on the same origin, not any user action. That drops it out of Critical. The coverage gap that remains — the suite only ever proves the migration works on data the test itself wrote in the correct shape, and the boot path has no guard if that assumption breaks — is a genuine Medium.
findings.reachability: Not reachable through the app. No shipped BookSum version writes a non-array under `booksum_library_*` (670b5fe:App.tsx:212) or a non-base64 `pdfData` (670b5fe:components/AddBookModal.tsx:28), and localStorage.setItem is atomic so partial writes are not a factor. Triggering it needs DevTools, an extension, or another app on the same origin writing a `booksum_library_`-prefixed key — plausible on a shared GitHub Pages origin, but not a user path. If it does happen the consequence is correctly analysed and severe: permanent spinner, unhandled rejection outside the error boundary, marker unwritten so it repeats on every reload.

plain.title: Every upgrade test uses perfectly-formed old data, so a startup-hanging failure passes green
plain.what: The tests for the upgrade from the previous version always seed flawless, correctly-shaped leftover data. Nothing damaged is ever tried.
plain.whyItMatters: The upgrade's worst failure mode — hanging the app on the loading screen forever — cannot be reproduced by any existing test, so it will not be caught by the suite.
plain.whatToDo: Add negative fixtures with damaged leftover data, and land them in the same change as the guards they are meant to prove.

findings.title: Migration test asserts summaryId but never the denormalised oneSentenceTakeaway it must move with
findings.description: The `splits each legacy book into a Book and a Summary` test (migrate.test.ts:88-106) asserts status, hasPdf, readingTimeMinutes and summaryId on the migrated Book but never asserts `oneSentenceTakeaway`, even though the fixture supplies it at line 33. That missing assertion is why the migration bug filed as F043 ships green. This is a test-coverage gap, not an independent defect — the producer is migrate.ts:105-119.
findings.verifierNote: Every factual claim verified, but this is the test-coverage view of F043 and must not carry high severity a second time. Confirmed by reading src/lib/storage/migrate.test.ts:88-106: the fixture supplies `oneSentenceTakeaway: 'Small changes compound.'` at line 33, the assertions at lines 97-101 cover status/hasPdf/readingTimeMinutes/summaryId/absence-of-pdfData, and there is no assertion on `atomic?.oneSentenceTakeaway` anywhere in the file. I ran `npx vitest run src/lib/storage/migrate.test.ts src/lib/storage/repo.test.ts` — 16/16 green, which is the proof: the suite is fully passing while the migrated Book genuinely lacks the field. But a missing assertion cannot itself produce a defect; the producer that drops the field is `books.create` at migrate.ts:105-119, filed as F043. Rating both at high double-counts one bug. Downgraded to medium: it is a real gap in the only test that covers the migration split, and it is exactly where the bug lives, so it is worth fixing — but the impact is 'the suite is green on a broken path', not a user-visible failure. Category left as-is; note that `discriminated-union-opportunity` is a poor fit for a test file — the union opportunity itself lives in src/types.ts:47-50 (F050).
findings.reachability: Not user-reachable — test code. The defect it fails to catch is reachable by any user who had legacy localStorage data: ProfileContext.tsx:31 runs migrateLegacyData() on boot, and every migrated book then renders 'Not summarised yet' at BookCard.tsx:89.
findings.blastRadius: 1 test file, 8 tests. The untested invariant (summaryId and oneSentenceTakeaway must be written together) governs the 14 non-test `books.*` call sites and every BookCard render.

plain.title: The migration test checks the summary link but not the headline that must travel with it
plain.what: The test that verifies old books are split correctly checks several fields, but not the short headline that list views need, even though the fixture contains one.
plain.whyItMatters: This is the exact omission that lets the 'Not summarised yet' bug ship green, and it is a one-line assertion away from being caught.
